units.leftText: The proverbs of Solomon, the son of David, king of Israel:
units.rightText: These are the proverbs of Solomon son of David, king of Israel,

units.leftText: to know wisdom and instruction; to discern the words of understanding;
units.rightText: for gaining wisdom and discipline, for comprehending words of insight,

units.leftText: to receive instruction in wise dealing, in righteousness, justice, and equity;
units.rightText: and for receiving instruction in wise living and in righteousness, justice, and equity.

units.leftText: to give prudence to the simple, knowledge and discretion to the young man—
units.rightText: To impart prudence to the simple and knowledge and discretion to the young,
rightNotes: 1:4 The Hebrew word rendered simple in Proverbs refers to one who is naive, without moral direction, or inclined to evil.

units.leftText: that the wise man may hear, and increase in learning; that the man of understanding may attain to sound counsel;
units.rightText: let the wise listen and gain instruction, and the discerning acquire wise counsel

units.leftText: to understand a proverb and parables, the words and riddles of the wise.
units.rightText: by understanding the proverbs and parables, the sayings and riddles of the wise.

units.leftText: The fear of the LORD is the beginning of knowledge, but the foolish despise wisdom and instruction.
units.rightText: The fear of the LORD is the beginning of knowledge, but fools despise wisdom and discipline. The Enticement of Sin
leftNotes: 1:7 When rendered in ALL CAPITAL LETTERS, “LORD” or “GOD” is the translation of God’s Proper Name (Hebrew “יהוה*”, usually pronounced Yahweh).
rightNotes: 1:7 The Hebrew words rendered as fool in Proverbs denote one who is morally deficient.

units.leftText: My son, listen to your father’s instruction, and don’t forsake your mother’s teaching;
units.rightText: Listen, my son, to your father’s instruction, and do not forsake the teaching of your mother.

units.leftText: for they will be a garland to grace your head, and chains around your neck.
units.rightText: For they are a garland of grace on your head and a pendant around your neck.

units.leftText: My son, if sinners entice you, don’t consent.
units.rightText: My son, if sinners entice you, do not yield to them.

units.leftText: If they say, “Come with us. Let’s lie in wait for blood. Let’s lurk secretly for the innocent without cause.
units.rightText: If they say, “Come along, let us lie in wait for blood, let us ambush the innocent without cause,

units.leftText: Let’s swallow them up alive like Sheol, and whole, like those who go down into the pit.
units.rightText: let us swallow them alive like Sheol, and whole like those descending into the Pit.
leftNotes: 1:12 Sheol is the place of the dead.

units.leftText: We’ll find all valuable wealth. We’ll fill our houses with plunder.
units.rightText: We will find all manner of precious goods; we will fill our houses with plunder.

units.leftText: You shall cast your lot among us. We’ll all have one purse”—
units.rightText: Throw in your lot with us; let us all share one purse” —

units.leftText: my son, don’t walk on the path with them. Keep your foot from their path,
units.rightText: my son, do not walk the road with them or set foot upon their path.

units.leftText: for their feet run to evil. They hurry to shed blood.
units.rightText: For their feet run to evil, and they are swift to shed blood.

units.leftText: For the net is spread in vain in the sight of any bird;
units.rightText: How futile it is to spread the net where any bird can see it!

units.leftText: but these lay in wait for their own blood. They lurk secretly for their own lives.
units.rightText: But they lie in wait for their own blood; they ambush their own lives.

units.leftText: So are the ways of everyone who is greedy for gain. It takes away the life of its owners.
units.rightText: Such is the fate of all who are greedy, whose unjust gain takes the lives of its possessors. Wisdom Calls Aloud

units.leftText: Wisdom calls aloud in the street. She utters her voice in the public squares.
units.rightText: Wisdom calls out in the street, she lifts her voice in the square;

units.leftText: She calls at the head of noisy places. At the entrance of the city gates, she utters her words:
units.rightText: in the main concourse she cries aloud, at the city gates she makes her speech:
rightNotes: 1:21 Or from the top of the wall

units.leftText: “How long, you simple ones, will you love simplicity? How long will mockers delight themselves in mockery, and fools hate knowledge?
units.rightText: “How long, O simple ones, will you love your simple ways? How long will scoffers delight in their scorn and fools hate knowledge?

units.leftText: Turn at my reproof. Behold, I will pour out my spirit on you. I will make known my words to you.
units.rightText: If you had repented at my rebuke, then surely I would have poured out my spirit on you; I would have made my words known to you.
leftNotes: 1:23 “Behold”, from “הִנֵּה*”, means look at, take notice, observe, see, or gaze at. It is often used as an interjection.

units.leftText: Because I have called, and you have refused; I have stretched out my hand, and no one has paid attention;
units.rightText: Because you refused my call, and no one took my outstretched hand,

units.leftText: but you have ignored all my counsel, and wanted none of my reproof;
units.rightText: because you neglected all my counsel, and wanted none of my correction,

units.leftText: I also will laugh at your disaster. I will mock when calamity overtakes you,
units.rightText: in turn I will mock your calamity; I will sneer when terror strikes you,

units.leftText: when calamity overtakes you like a storm, when your disaster comes on like a whirlwind, when distress and anguish come on you.
units.rightText: when your dread comes like a storm, and your destruction like a whirlwind, when distress and anguish overwhelm you.

units.leftText: Then they will call on me, but I will not answer. They will seek me diligently, but they will not find me,
units.rightText: Then they will call on me, but I will not answer; they will earnestly seek me, but will not find me.

units.leftText: because they hated knowledge, and didn’t choose the fear of the LORD.
units.rightText: For they hated knowledge and chose not to fear the LORD.

units.leftText: They wanted none of my counsel. They despised all my reproof.
units.rightText: They accepted none of my counsel; they despised all my reproof.

units.leftText: Therefore they will eat of the fruit of their own way, and be filled with their own schemes.
units.rightText: So they will eat the fruit of their own way, and be filled with their own devices.

units.leftText: For the backsliding of the simple will kill them. The careless ease of fools will destroy them.
units.rightText: For the waywardness of the simple will slay them, and the complacency of fools will destroy them.

units.leftText: But whoever listens to me will dwell securely, and will be at ease, without fear of harm.”
units.rightText: But whoever listens to me will dwell in safety, secure from the fear of evil.”

units.leftText: My son, if you will receive my words, and store up my commandments within you,
units.rightText: My son, if you accept my words and hide my commandments within you,

units.leftText: so as to turn your ear to wisdom, and apply your heart to understanding;
units.rightText: if you incline your ear to wisdom and direct your heart to understanding,

units.leftText: yes, if you call out for discernment, and lift up your voice for understanding;
units.rightText: if you truly call out to insight and lift your voice to understanding,

units.leftText: if you seek her as silver, and search for her as for hidden treasures;
units.rightText: if you seek it like silver and search it out like hidden treasure,

units.leftText: then you will understand the fear of the LORD, and find the knowledge of God.
units.rightText: then you will discern the fear of the LORD and discover the knowledge of God.

units.leftText: For the LORD gives wisdom. Out of his mouth comes knowledge and understanding.
units.rightText: For the LORD gives wisdom; from His mouth come knowledge and understanding.

units.leftText: He lays up sound wisdom for the upright. He is a shield to those who walk in integrity,
units.rightText: He stores up sound wisdom for the upright; He is a shield to those who walk with integrity,

units.leftText: that he may guard the paths of justice, and preserve the way of his saints.
units.rightText: to guard the paths of justice and protect the way of His saints.

units.leftText: Then you will understand righteousness and justice, equity and every good path.
units.rightText: Then you will discern righteousness and justice and equity— every good path.

units.leftText: For wisdom will enter into your heart. Knowledge will be pleasant to your soul.
units.rightText: For wisdom will enter your heart, and knowledge will delight your soul.

units.leftText: Discretion will watch over you. Understanding will keep you,
units.rightText: Discretion will watch over you, and understanding will guard you,

units.leftText: to deliver you from the way of evil, from the men who speak perverse things,
units.rightText: to deliver you from the way of evil, from the man who speaks perversity,

units.leftText: who forsake the paths of uprightness, to walk in the ways of darkness,
units.rightText: from those who leave the straight paths to walk in the ways of darkness,

units.leftText: who rejoice to do evil, and delight in the perverseness of evil,
units.rightText: from those who enjoy doing evil and rejoice in the twistedness of evil,

units.leftText: who are crooked in their ways, and wayward in their paths,
units.rightText: whose paths are crooked and whose ways are devious.

units.leftText: to deliver you from the strange woman, even from the foreigner who flatters with her words,
units.rightText: It will rescue you from the forbidden woman, from the stranger with seductive words
rightNotes: 2:16 Or wayward wife
2:16 Or adulteress

units.leftText: who forsakes the friend of her youth, and forgets the covenant of her God;
units.rightText: who abandons the partner of her youth and forgets the covenant of her God.

units.leftText: for her house leads down to death, her paths to the departed spirits.
units.rightText: For her house sinks down to death, and her tracks to the departed spirits.
rightNotes: 2:18 Hebrew to the Rephaim

units.leftText: None who go to her return again, neither do they attain to the paths of life.
units.rightText: None who go to her return or negotiate the paths of life.

units.leftText: Therefore walk in the way of good men, and keep the paths of the righteous.
units.rightText: So you will follow in the ways of the good, and keep to the paths of the righteous.

units.leftText: For the upright will dwell in the land. The perfect will remain in it.
units.rightText: For the upright will inhabit the land, and the blameless will remain in it;

units.leftText: But the wicked will be cut off from the land. The treacherous will be rooted out of it.
units.rightText: but the wicked will be cut off from the land, and the unfaithful will be uprooted.

units.leftText: My son, don’t forget my teaching, but let your heart keep my commandments,
units.rightText: My son, do not forget my teaching, but let your heart keep my commandments;

units.leftText: for they will add to you length of days, years of life, and peace.
units.rightText: for they will add length to your days, years and peace to your life.

units.leftText: Don’t let kindness and truth forsake you. Bind them around your neck. Write them on the tablet of your heart.
units.rightText: Never let loving devotion or faithfulness leave you; bind them around your neck, write them on the tablet of your heart.
rightNotes: 3:3 Forms of the Hebrew chesed are translated here and in most cases throughout the Scriptures as loving devotion; the range of meaning includes love, goodness, kindness, faithfulness, and mercy, as well as loyalty to a covenant.

units.leftText: So you will find favor, and good understanding in the sight of God and man.
units.rightText: Then you will find favor and high regard in the sight of God and man.

units.leftText: Trust in the LORD with all your heart, and don’t lean on your own understanding.
units.rightText: Trust in the LORD with all your heart, and lean not on your own understanding;

units.leftText: In all your ways acknowledge him, and he will make your paths straight.
units.rightText: in all your ways acknowledge Him, and He will make your paths straight.

units.leftText: Don’t be wise in your own eyes. Fear the LORD, and depart from evil.
units.rightText: Be not wise in your own eyes; fear the LORD and turn away from evil.

units.leftText: It will be health to your body, and nourishment to your bones.
units.rightText: This will bring healing to your body and refreshment to your bones.
rightNotes: 3:8 Hebrew navel
3:8 Or medicine

units.leftText: Honor the LORD with your substance, with the first fruits of all your increase;
units.rightText: Honor the LORD with your wealth and with the firstfruits of all your crops;

units.leftText: so your barns will be filled with plenty, and your vats will overflow with new wine.
units.rightText: then your barns will be filled with plenty, and your vats will overflow with new wine.

units.leftText: My son, don’t despise the LORD’s discipline, neither be weary of his correction;
units.rightText: My son, do not reject the discipline of the LORD, and do not loathe His rebuke;
rightNotes: 3:11 LXX and do not lose heart when He rebukes; cited in Hebrews 12:5|HEB 12:5*

units.leftText: for whom the LORD loves, he corrects, even as a father reproves the son in whom he delights.
units.rightText: for the LORD disciplines the one He loves, as does a father the son in whom he delights. The Blessings of Wisdom
rightNotes: 3:12 LXX and He flogs every son He receives; cited in Hebrews 12:6|HEB 12:6*

units.leftText: Happy is the man who finds wisdom, the man who gets understanding.
units.rightText: Blessed is the man who finds wisdom, the man who acquires understanding,

units.leftText: For her good profit is better than getting silver, and her return is better than fine gold.
units.rightText: for she is more profitable than silver, and her gain is better than fine gold.

units.leftText: She is more precious than rubies. None of the things you can desire are to be compared to her.
units.rightText: She is more precious than rubies; nothing you desire compares with her.

units.leftText: Length of days is in her right hand. In her left hand are riches and honor.
units.rightText: Long life is in her right hand; in her left hand are riches and honor.

units.leftText: Her ways are ways of pleasantness. All her paths are peace.
units.rightText: All her ways are pleasant, and all her paths are peaceful.

units.leftText: She is a tree of life to those who lay hold of her. Happy is everyone who retains her.
units.rightText: She is a tree of life to those who embrace her, and those who lay hold of her are blessed.

units.leftText: By wisdom the LORD founded the earth. By understanding, he established the heavens.
units.rightText: The LORD founded the earth by wisdom and established the heavens by understanding.

units.leftText: By his knowledge, the depths were broken up, and the skies drop down the dew.
units.rightText: By His knowledge the watery depths were broken open, and the clouds dripped with dew.

units.leftText: My son, let them not depart from your eyes. Keep sound wisdom and discretion,
units.rightText: My son, do not lose sight of this: Preserve sound judgment and discernment.

units.leftText: so they will be life to your soul, and grace for your neck.
units.rightText: They will be life to your soul and adornment to your neck.

units.leftText: Then you shall walk in your way securely. Your foot won’t stumble.
units.rightText: Then you will go on your way in safety, and your foot will not stumble.

units.leftText: When you lie down, you will not be afraid. Yes, you will lie down, and your sleep will be sweet.
units.rightText: When you lie down, you will not be afraid; when you rest, your sleep will be sweet.

units.leftText: Don’t be afraid of sudden fear, neither of the desolation of the wicked, when it comes;
units.rightText: Do not fear sudden danger or the ruin that overtakes the wicked,

units.leftText: for the LORD will be your confidence, and will keep your foot from being taken.
units.rightText: for the LORD will be your confidence and will keep your foot from the snare.

units.leftText: Don’t withhold good from those to whom it is due, when it is in the power of your hand to do it.
units.rightText: Do not withhold good from the deserving when it is within your power to act.
rightNotes: 3:27 Or from its owners

units.leftText: Don’t say to your neighbor, “Go, and come again; tomorrow I will give it to you,” when you have it by you.
units.rightText: Do not tell your neighbor, “Come back tomorrow and I will provide”— when you already have the means.

units.leftText: Don’t devise evil against your neighbor, since he dwells securely by you.
units.rightText: Do not devise evil against your neighbor, for he trustfully dwells beside you.

units.leftText: Don’t strive with a man without cause, if he has done you no harm.
units.rightText: Do not accuse a man without cause, when he has done you no harm.

units.leftText: Don’t envy the man of violence. Choose none of his ways.
units.rightText: Do not envy a violent man or choose any of his ways;

units.leftText: For the perverse is an abomination to the LORD, but his friendship is with the upright.
units.rightText: for the LORD detests the perverse, but He is a friend to the upright.

units.leftText: The LORD’s curse is in the house of the wicked, but he blesses the habitation of the righteous.
units.rightText: The curse of the LORD is on the house of the wicked, but He blesses the home of the righteous.

units.leftText: Surely he mocks the mockers, but he gives grace to the humble.
units.rightText: He mocks the mockers, but gives grace to the humble.
rightNotes: 3:34 LXX The Lord opposes the proud, but gives grace to the humble; cited in James 4:6|JAS 4:6* and 1 Peter 5:5

units.leftText: The wise will inherit glory, but shame will be the promotion of fools.
units.rightText: The wise will inherit honor, but fools are held up to shame.

units.leftText: Listen, sons, to a father’s instruction. Pay attention and know understanding;
units.rightText: Listen, my sons, to a father’s instruction; pay attention and gain understanding.

units.leftText: for I give you sound learning. Don’t forsake my law.
units.rightText: For I give you sound teaching; do not abandon my directive.

units.leftText: For I was a son to my father, tender and an only child in the sight of my mother.
units.rightText: When I was a son to my father, tender and the only child of my mother,

units.leftText: He taught me, and said to me: “Let your heart retain my words. Keep my commandments, and live.
units.rightText: he taught me and said, “Let your heart lay hold of my words; keep my commands and you will live.

units.leftText: Get wisdom. Get understanding. Don’t forget, and don’t deviate from the words of my mouth.
units.rightText: Get wisdom, get understanding; do not forget my words or turn from them.

units.leftText: Don’t forsake her, and she will preserve you. Love her, and she will keep you.
units.rightText: Do not forsake wisdom, and she will preserve you; love her, and she will guard you.

units.leftText: Wisdom is supreme. Get wisdom. Yes, though it costs all your possessions, get understanding.
units.rightText: Wisdom is supreme; so acquire wisdom. And whatever you may acquire, gain understanding.
rightNotes: 4:7 Or And whatever else you acquire

units.leftText: Esteem her, and she will exalt you. She will bring you to honor when you embrace her.
units.rightText: Prize her, and she will exalt you; if you embrace her, she will honor you.

units.leftText: She will give to your head a garland of grace. She will deliver a crown of splendor to you.”
units.rightText: She will set a garland of grace on your head; she will present you with a crown of beauty.”

units.leftText: Listen, my son, and receive my sayings. The years of your life will be many.
units.rightText: Listen, my son, and receive my words, and the years of your life will be many.

units.leftText: I have taught you in the way of wisdom. I have led you in straight paths.
units.rightText: I will guide you in the way of wisdom; I will lead you on straight paths.

units.leftText: When you go, your steps will not be hampered. When you run, you will not stumble.
units.rightText: When you walk, your steps will not be impeded; when you run, you will not stumble.

units.leftText: Take firm hold of instruction. Don’t let her go. Keep her, for she is your life.
units.rightText: Hold on to instruction; do not let go. Guard it, for it is your life.

units.leftText: Don’t enter into the path of the wicked. Don’t walk in the way of evil men.
units.rightText: Do not set foot on the path of the wicked or walk in the way of evildoers.

units.leftText: Avoid it, and don’t pass by it. Turn from it, and pass on.
units.rightText: Avoid it; do not travel on it. Turn from it and pass on by.

units.leftText: For they don’t sleep unless they do evil. Their sleep is taken away, unless they make someone fall.
units.rightText: For they cannot sleep unless they do evil; they are deprived of slumber until they make someone fall.

units.leftText: For they eat the bread of wickedness and drink the wine of violence.
units.rightText: For they eat the bread of wickedness and drink the wine of violence.

units.leftText: But the path of the righteous is like the dawning light that shines more and more until the perfect day.
units.rightText: The path of the righteous is like the first gleam of dawn, shining brighter and brighter until midday.

units.leftText: The way of the wicked is like darkness. They don’t know what they stumble over.
units.rightText: But the way of the wicked is like the darkest gloom; they do not know what makes them stumble.

units.leftText: My son, attend to my words. Turn your ear to my sayings.
units.rightText: My son, pay attention to my words; incline your ear to my sayings.

units.leftText: Let them not depart from your eyes. Keep them in the center of your heart.
units.rightText: Do not lose sight of them; keep them within your heart.

units.leftText: For they are life to those who find them, and health to their whole body.
units.rightText: For they are life to those who find them, and health to the whole body.

units.leftText: Keep your heart with all diligence, for out of it is the wellspring of life.
units.rightText: Guard your heart with all diligence, for from it flow springs of life.

units.leftText: Put away from yourself a perverse mouth. Put corrupt lips far from you.
units.rightText: Put away deception from your mouth; keep your lips from perverse speech.

units.leftText: Let your eyes look straight ahead. Fix your gaze directly before you.
units.rightText: Let your eyes look forward; fix your gaze straight ahead.

units.leftText: Make the path of your feet level. Let all of your ways be established.
units.rightText: Make a level path for your feet, and all your ways will be sure.
rightNotes: 4:26 Or Ponder the path for your feet; LXX Make straight paths for your feet; cited in Hebrews 12:13|HEB 12:13*

units.leftText: Don’t turn to the right hand nor to the left. Remove your foot from evil.
units.rightText: Do not swerve to the right or to the left; turn your feet away from evil.

units.leftText: My son, pay attention to my wisdom. Turn your ear to my understanding,
units.rightText: My son, pay attention to my wisdom; incline your ear to my insight,

units.leftText: that you may maintain discretion, that your lips may preserve knowledge.
units.rightText: that you may maintain discretion and your lips may preserve knowledge.

units.leftText: For the lips of an adulteress drip honey. Her mouth is smoother than oil,
units.rightText: Though the lips of the forbidden woman drip honey and her speech is smoother than oil,
rightNotes: 5:3 Or the adulteress
5:3 Or her palate

units.leftText: but in the end she is as bitter as wormwood, and as sharp as a two-edged sword.
units.rightText: in the end she is bitter as wormwood, sharp as a double-edged sword.

units.leftText: Her feet go down to death. Her steps lead straight to Sheol.
units.rightText: Her feet go down to death; her steps lead straight to Sheol.
leftNotes: 5:5 Sheol is the place of the dead.
rightNotes: 5:5 Or lay hold of Sheol

units.leftText: She gives no thought to the way of life. Her ways are crooked, and she doesn’t know it.
units.rightText: She does not consider the path of life; she does not know that her ways are unstable.

units.leftText: Now therefore, my sons, listen to me. Don’t depart from the words of my mouth.
units.rightText: So now, my sons, listen to me, and do not turn aside from the words of my mouth.

units.leftText: Remove your way far from her. Don’t come near the door of her house,
units.rightText: Keep your path far from her; do not go near the door of her house,

units.leftText: lest you give your honor to others, and your years to the cruel one;
units.rightText: lest you concede your vigor to others, and your years to one who is cruel;

units.leftText: lest strangers feast on your wealth, and your labors enrich another man’s house.
units.rightText: lest strangers feast on your wealth, and your labors enrich the house of a foreigner.

units.leftText: You will groan at your latter end, when your flesh and your body are consumed,
units.rightText: At the end of your life you will groan when your flesh and your body are spent,

units.leftText: and say, “How I have hated instruction, and my heart despised reproof.
units.rightText: and you will say, “How I hated discipline, and my heart despised reproof!

units.leftText: I haven’t obeyed the voice of my teachers, nor turned my ear to those who instructed me!
units.rightText: I did not listen to the voice of my teachers or incline my ear to my mentors.

units.leftText: I have come to the brink of utter ruin, among the gathered assembly.”
units.rightText: I am on the brink of utter ruin in the midst of the whole assembly.”

units.leftText: Drink water out of your own cistern, running water out of your own well.
units.rightText: Drink water from your own cistern, and running water from your own well.

units.leftText: Should your springs overflow in the streets, streams of water in the public squares?
units.rightText: Why should your springs flow in the streets, your streams of water in the public squares?

units.leftText: Let them be for yourself alone, not for strangers with you.
units.rightText: Let them be yours alone, never to be shared with strangers.

units.leftText: Let your spring be blessed. Rejoice in the wife of your youth.
units.rightText: May your fountain be blessed, and may you rejoice in the wife of your youth:

units.leftText: A loving doe and a graceful deer— let her breasts satisfy you at all times. Be captivated always with her love.
units.rightText: A loving doe, a graceful fawn— may her breasts satisfy you always; may you be captivated by her love forever.
rightNotes: 5:19 Or be led astray; also in verse 20

units.leftText: For why should you, my son, be captivated with an adulteress? Why embrace the bosom of another?
units.rightText: Why be captivated, my son, by an adulteress, or embrace the bosom of a stranger?
rightNotes: 5:20 Or a foreign woman or another man’s wife

units.leftText: For the ways of man are before the LORD’s eyes. He examines all his paths.
units.rightText: For a man’s ways are before the eyes of the LORD, and the LORD examines all his paths.
rightNotes: 5:21 Or ponders or makes level

units.leftText: The evil deeds of the wicked ensnare him. The cords of his sin hold him firmly.
units.rightText: The iniquities of a wicked man entrap him; the cords of his sin entangle him.

units.leftText: He will die for lack of instruction. In the greatness of his folly, he will go astray.
units.rightText: He dies for lack of discipline, led astray by his own great folly.

units.leftText: My son, if you have become collateral for your neighbor, if you have struck your hands in pledge for a stranger,
units.rightText: My son, if you have put up security for your neighbor, if you have struck hands in pledge with a stranger,

units.leftText: you are trapped by the words of your mouth; you are ensnared with the words of your mouth.
units.rightText: if you have been trapped by the words of your lips, ensnared by the words of your mouth,

units.leftText: Do this now, my son, and deliver yourself, since you have come into the hand of your neighbor. Go, humble yourself. Press your plea with your neighbor.
units.rightText: then do this, my son, to free yourself, for you have fallen into your neighbor’s hands: Go, humble yourself, and press your plea with your neighbor.
rightNotes: 6:3 Or hasten

units.leftText: Give no sleep to your eyes, nor slumber to your eyelids.
units.rightText: Allow no sleep to your eyes or slumber to your eyelids.

units.leftText: Free yourself, like a gazelle from the hand of the hunter, like a bird from the snare of the fowler.
units.rightText: Free yourself, like a gazelle from the hand of the hunter, like a bird from the snare of the fowler.
rightNotes: 6:5 Hebrew does not include of the hunter.

units.leftText: Go to the ant, you sluggard. Consider her ways, and be wise;
units.rightText: Walk in the manner of the ant, O slacker; observe its ways and become wise.

units.leftText: which having no chief, overseer, or ruler,
units.rightText: Without a commander, without an overseer or ruler,

units.leftText: provides her bread in the summer, and gathers her food in the harvest.
units.rightText: it prepares its provisions in summer; it gathers its food at harvest.

units.leftText: How long will you sleep, sluggard? When will you arise out of your sleep?
units.rightText: How long will you lie there, O slacker? When will you get up from your sleep?

units.leftText: A little sleep, a little slumber, a little folding of the hands to sleep—
units.rightText: A little sleep, a little slumber, a little folding of the hands to rest,

units.leftText: so your poverty will come as a robber, and your scarcity as an armed man.
units.rightText: and poverty will come upon you like a robber, and need like a bandit.

units.leftText: A worthless person, a man of iniquity, is he who walks with a perverse mouth,
units.rightText: A worthless person, a wicked man, walks with a perverse mouth,

units.leftText: who winks with his eyes, who signals with his feet, who motions with his fingers,
units.rightText: winking his eyes, speaking with his feet, and pointing with his fingers.

units.leftText: in whose heart is perverseness, who devises evil continually, who always sows discord.
units.rightText: With deceit in his heart he devises evil; he continually sows discord.

units.leftText: Therefore his calamity will come suddenly. He will be broken suddenly, and that without remedy.
units.rightText: Therefore calamity will come upon him suddenly; in an instant he will be shattered beyond recovery.

units.leftText: There are six things which the LORD hates; yes, seven which are an abomination to him:
units.rightText: There are six things that the LORD hates, seven that are detestable to Him:

units.leftText: arrogant eyes, a lying tongue, hands that shed innocent blood,
units.rightText: haughty eyes, a lying tongue, hands that shed innocent blood,

units.leftText: a heart that devises wicked schemes, feet that are swift in running to mischief,
units.rightText: a heart that devises wicked schemes, feet that run swiftly to evil,

units.leftText: a false witness who utters lies, and he who sows discord among brothers.
units.rightText: a false witness who gives false testimony, and one who stirs up discord among brothers. Warnings against Adultery

units.leftText: My son, keep your father’s commandment, and don’t forsake your mother’s teaching.
units.rightText: My son, keep your father’s commandment, and do not forsake your mother’s teaching.

units.leftText: Bind them continually on your heart. Tie them around your neck.
units.rightText: Bind them always upon your heart; tie them around your neck.

units.leftText: When you walk, it will lead you. When you sleep, it will watch over you. When you awake, it will talk with you.
units.rightText: When you walk, they will guide you; when you lie down, they will watch over you; when you awake, they will speak to you.

units.leftText: For the commandment is a lamp, and the law is light. Reproofs of instruction are the way of life,
units.rightText: For this commandment is a lamp, this teaching is a light, and the reproofs of discipline are the way to life,

units.leftText: to keep you from the immoral woman, from the flattery of the wayward wife’s tongue.
units.rightText: to keep you from the evil woman, from the smooth tongue of the adulteress.
rightNotes: 6:24 Or the stranger

units.leftText: Don’t lust after her beauty in your heart, neither let her captivate you with her eyelids.
units.rightText: Do not lust in your heart for her beauty or let her captivate you with her eyes.
rightNotes: 6:25 Or eyelids or eyelashes

units.leftText: For a prostitute reduces you to a piece of bread. The adulteress hunts for your precious life.
units.rightText: For the levy of the prostitute is poverty, and the adulteress preys upon your very life.
rightNotes: 6:26 Literally a crust of bread

units.leftText: Can a man scoop fire into his lap, and his clothes not be burned?
units.rightText: Can a man embrace fire and his clothes not be burned?

units.leftText: Or can one walk on hot coals, and his feet not be scorched?
units.rightText: Can a man walk on hot coals without scorching his feet?

units.leftText: So is he who goes in to his neighbor’s wife. Whoever touches her will not be unpunished.
units.rightText: So is he who sleeps with another man’s wife; no one who touches her will go unpunished.

units.leftText: Men don’t despise a thief if he steals to satisfy himself when he is hungry,
units.rightText: Men do not despise the thief if he steals to satisfy his hunger.

units.leftText: but if he is found, he shall restore seven times. He shall give all the wealth of his house.
units.rightText: Yet if caught, he must pay sevenfold; he must give up all the wealth of his house.

units.leftText: He who commits adultery with a woman is void of understanding. He who does it destroys his own soul.
units.rightText: He who commits adultery lacks judgment; whoever does so destroys himself.

units.leftText: He will get wounds and dishonor. His reproach will not be wiped away.
units.rightText: Wounds and dishonor will befall him, and his reproach will never be wiped away.

units.leftText: For jealousy arouses the fury of the husband. He won’t spare in the day of vengeance.
units.rightText: For jealousy enrages a husband, and he will show no mercy in the day of vengeance.

units.leftText: He won’t regard any ransom, neither will he rest content, though you give many gifts.
units.rightText: He will not be appeased by any ransom, or persuaded by lavish gifts.

units.leftText: My son, keep my words. Lay up my commandments within you.
units.rightText: My son, keep my words and treasure my commandments within you.

units.leftText: Keep my commandments and live! Guard my teaching as the apple of your eye.
units.rightText: Keep my commandments and live; guard my teachings as the apple of your eye.
rightNotes: 7:2 Literally the pupil

units.leftText: Bind them on your fingers. Write them on the tablet of your heart.
units.rightText: Tie them to your fingers; write them on the tablet of your heart.

units.leftText: Tell wisdom, “You are my sister.” Call understanding your relative,
units.rightText: Say to wisdom, “You are my sister,” and call understanding your kinsman,

units.leftText: that they may keep you from the strange woman, from the foreigner who flatters with her words.
units.rightText: that they may keep you from the adulteress, from the stranger with seductive words.

units.leftText: For at the window of my house, I looked out through my lattice.
units.rightText: For at the window of my house I looked through the lattice.

units.leftText: I saw among the simple ones. I discerned among the youths a young man void of understanding,
units.rightText: I saw among the simple, I noticed among the youths, a young man lacking judgment,

units.leftText: passing through the street near her corner, he went the way to her house,
units.rightText: crossing the street near her corner, strolling down the road to her house,

units.leftText: in the twilight, in the evening of the day, in the middle of the night and in the darkness.
units.rightText: at twilight, as the day was fading into the dark of the night.

units.leftText: Behold, there a woman met him with the attire of a prostitute, and with crafty intent.
units.rightText: Then a woman came out to meet him, with the attire of a harlot and cunning of heart.

units.leftText: She is loud and defiant. Her feet don’t stay in her house.
units.rightText: She is loud and defiant; her feet do not remain at home.

units.leftText: Now she is in the streets, now in the squares, and lurking at every corner.
units.rightText: Now in the street, now in the squares, she lurks at every corner.

units.leftText: So she caught him, and kissed him. With an impudent face she said to him:
units.rightText: She seizes him and kisses him; she brazenly says to him:

units.leftText: “Sacrifices of peace offerings are with me. Today I have paid my vows.
units.rightText: “I have made my peace offerings; today I have paid my vows.

units.leftText: Therefore I came out to meet you, to diligently seek your face, and I have found you.
units.rightText: So I came out to meet you; I sought you, and I have found you.

units.leftText: I have spread my couch with carpets of tapestry, with striped cloths of the yarn of Egypt.
units.rightText: I have decked my bed with coverings, with colored linen from Egypt.

units.leftText: I have perfumed my bed with myrrh, aloes, and cinnamon.
units.rightText: I have perfumed my bed with myrrh, with aloes, and with cinnamon.

units.leftText: Come, let’s take our fill of loving until the morning. Let’s solace ourselves with loving.
units.rightText: Come, let us take our fill of love till morning. Let us delight in loving caresses!

units.leftText: For my husband isn’t at home. He has gone on a long journey.
units.rightText: For my husband is not at home; he has gone on a long journey.

units.leftText: He has taken a bag of money with him. He will come home at the full moon.”
units.rightText: He took with him a bag of money and will not return till the moon is full.”

units.leftText: With persuasive words, she led him astray. With the flattering of her lips, she seduced him.
units.rightText: With her great persuasion she entices him; with her flattering lips she lures him.

units.leftText: He followed her immediately, as an ox goes to the slaughter, as a fool stepping into a noose.
units.rightText: He follows her on impulse, like an ox going to the slaughter, like a deer bounding into a trap,
rightNotes: 7:22 Probable reading (see LXX, Vulgate, Syriac); Hebrew like fetters to discipline a fool

units.leftText: Until an arrow strikes through his liver, as a bird hurries to the snare, and doesn’t know that it will cost his life.
units.rightText: until an arrow pierces his liver, like a bird darting into a snare— not knowing it will cost him his life.

units.leftText: Now therefore, sons, listen to me. Pay attention to the words of my mouth.
units.rightText: Now, my sons, listen to me, and attend to the words of my mouth.

units.leftText: Don’t let your heart turn to her ways. Don’t go astray in her paths,
units.rightText: Do not let your heart turn aside to her ways; do not stray into her paths.

units.leftText: for she has thrown down many wounded. Yes, all her slain are a mighty army.
units.rightText: For she has brought many down to death; her slain are many in number.

units.leftText: Her house is the way to Sheol, going down to the rooms of death.
units.rightText: Her house is the road to Sheol, descending to the chambers of death.
leftNotes: 7:27 Sheol is the place of the dead.

units.leftText: Doesn’t wisdom cry out? Doesn’t understanding raise her voice?
units.rightText: Does not wisdom call out, and understanding raise her voice?

units.leftText: On the top of high places by the way, where the paths meet, she stands.
units.rightText: On the heights overlooking the road, at the crossroads she takes her stand.

units.leftText: Beside the gates, at the entry of the city, at the entry doors, she cries aloud:
units.rightText: Beside the gates to the city, at the entrances she cries out:

units.leftText: “I call to you men! I send my voice to the sons of mankind.
units.rightText: “To you, O men, I call out, and my cry is to the sons of men.

units.leftText: You simple, understand prudence! You fools, be of an understanding heart!
units.rightText: O simple ones, learn to be shrewd; O fools, gain understanding.
rightNotes: 8:5 Or instruct your minds

units.leftText: Hear, for I will speak excellent things. The opening of my lips is for right things.
units.rightText: Listen, for I speak of noble things, and the opening of my lips will reveal right.

units.leftText: For my mouth speaks truth. Wickedness is an abomination to my lips.
units.rightText: For my mouth will speak the truth, and wickedness is detestable to my lips.

units.leftText: All the words of my mouth are in righteousness. There is nothing crooked or perverse in them.
units.rightText: All the words of my mouth are righteous; none are crooked or perverse.

units.leftText: They are all plain to him who understands, right to those who find knowledge.
units.rightText: They are all plain to the discerning, and upright to those who find knowledge.

units.leftText: Receive my instruction rather than silver, knowledge rather than choice gold.
units.rightText: Receive my instruction instead of silver, and knowledge rather than pure gold.

units.leftText: For wisdom is better than rubies. All the things that may be desired can’t be compared to it.
units.rightText: For wisdom is more precious than rubies, and nothing you desire compares with her.

units.leftText: “I, wisdom, have made prudence my dwelling. Find out knowledge and discretion.
units.rightText: I, wisdom, dwell together with prudence, and I find knowledge and discretion.

units.leftText: The fear of the LORD is to hate evil. I hate pride, arrogance, the evil way, and the perverse mouth.
units.rightText: To fear the LORD is to hate evil; I hate arrogant pride, evil conduct, and perverse speech.

units.leftText: Counsel and sound knowledge are mine. I have understanding and power.
units.rightText: Counsel and sound judgment are mine; I have insight and strength.

units.leftText: By me kings reign, and princes decree justice.
units.rightText: By me kings reign, and rulers enact just laws;

units.leftText: By me princes rule, nobles, and all the righteous rulers of the earth.
units.rightText: By me princes rule, and all nobles who govern justly.
rightNotes: 8:16 Some Hebrew manuscripts and LXX who govern the earth

units.leftText: I love those who love me. Those who seek me diligently will find me.
units.rightText: I love those who love me, and those who seek me early shall find me.

units.leftText: With me are riches, honor, enduring wealth, and prosperity.
units.rightText: With me are riches and honor, enduring wealth and righteousness.

units.leftText: My fruit is better than gold, yes, than fine gold, my yield than choice silver.
units.rightText: My fruit is better than gold, pure gold, and my harvest surpasses choice silver.

units.leftText: I walk in the way of righteousness, in the middle of the paths of justice,
units.rightText: I walk in the way of righteousness, along the paths of justice,

units.leftText: that I may give wealth to those who love me. I fill their treasuries.
units.rightText: bestowing wealth on those who love me and making their treasuries full.

units.leftText: “The LORD possessed me in the beginning of his work, before his deeds of old.
units.rightText: The LORD created me as His first course, before His works of old.
rightNotes: 8:22 Or The LORD possessed me at the beginning of His way

units.leftText: I was set up from everlasting, from the beginning, before the earth existed.
units.rightText: From everlasting I was established, from the beginning, before the earth began.

units.leftText: When there were no depths, I was born, when there were no springs abounding with water.
units.rightText: When there were no watery depths, I was brought forth, when no springs were overflowing with water.

units.leftText: Before the mountains were settled in place, before the hills, I was born;
units.rightText: Before the mountains were settled, before the hills, I was brought forth,

units.leftText: while as yet he had not made the earth, nor the fields, nor the beginning of the dust of the world.
units.rightText: before He made the land or fields, or any of the dust of the earth.

units.leftText: When he established the heavens, I was there. When he set a circle on the surface of the deep,
units.rightText: I was there when He established the heavens, when He inscribed a circle on the face of the deep,

units.leftText: when he established the clouds above, when the springs of the deep became strong,
units.rightText: when He established the clouds above, when the fountains of the deep gushed forth,

units.leftText: when he gave to the sea its boundary, that the waters should not violate his commandment, when he marked out the foundations of the earth,
units.rightText: when He set a boundary for the sea, so that the waters would not surpass His command, when He marked out the foundations of the earth.

units.leftText: then I was the craftsman by his side. I was a delight day by day, always rejoicing before him,
units.rightText: Then I was a skilled craftsman at His side, and His delight day by day, rejoicing always in His presence.
rightNotes: 8:30 Or filled with His delight

units.leftText: rejoicing in his whole world. My delight was with the sons of men.
units.rightText: I was rejoicing in His whole world, delighting together in the sons of men.

units.leftText: “Now therefore, my sons, listen to me, for blessed are those who keep my ways.
units.rightText: Now therefore, my sons, listen to me, for blessed are those who keep my ways.

units.leftText: Hear instruction, and be wise. Don’t refuse it.
units.rightText: Listen to instruction and be wise; do not ignore it.

units.leftText: Blessed is the man who hears me, watching daily at my gates, waiting at my door posts.
units.rightText: Blessed is the man who listens to me, watching daily at my doors, waiting at the posts of my doorway.

units.leftText: For whoever finds me finds life, and will obtain favor from the LORD.
units.rightText: For whoever finds me finds life and obtains the favor of the LORD.

units.leftText: But he who sins against me wrongs his own soul. All those who hate me love death.”
units.rightText: But he who fails to find me harms himself; all who hate me love death.”

units.leftText: Wisdom has built her house. She has carved out her seven pillars.
units.rightText: Wisdom has built her house; she has carved out her seven pillars.
rightNotes: 9:1 Hebrew; LXX, Syriac, and Aramaic Targum has set up

units.leftText: She has prepared her meat. She has mixed her wine. She has also set her table.
units.rightText: She has prepared her meat and mixed her wine; she has also set her table.

units.leftText: She has sent out her maidens. She cries from the highest places of the city:
units.rightText: She has sent out her maidservants; she calls out from the heights of the city.

units.leftText: “Whoever is simple, let him turn in here!” As for him who is void of understanding, she says to him,
units.rightText: “Whoever is simple, let him turn in here!” she says to him who lacks judgment.

units.leftText: “Come, eat some of my bread, Drink some of the wine which I have mixed!
units.rightText: “Come, eat my bread and drink the wine I have mixed.

units.leftText: Leave your simple ways, and live. Walk in the way of understanding.”
units.rightText: Leave your folly behind, and you will live; walk in the way of understanding.”

units.leftText: One who corrects a mocker invites insult. One who reproves a wicked man invites abuse.
units.rightText: He who corrects a mocker brings shame on himself; he who rebukes a wicked man taints himself.

units.leftText: Don’t reprove a scoffer, lest he hate you. Reprove a wise person, and he will love you.
units.rightText: Do not rebuke a mocker, or he will hate you; rebuke a wise man, and he will love you.

units.leftText: Instruct a wise person, and he will be still wiser. Teach a righteous person, and he will increase in learning.
units.rightText: Instruct a wise man, and he will be wiser still; teach a righteous man, and he will increase his learning.

units.leftText: The fear of the LORD is the beginning of wisdom. The knowledge of the Holy One is understanding.
units.rightText: The fear of the LORD is the beginning of wisdom, and knowledge of the Holy One is understanding.

units.leftText: For by me your days will be multiplied. The years of your life will be increased.
units.rightText: For through wisdom your days will be multiplied, and years will be added to your life.
rightNotes: 9:11 LXX, Syriac, and Aramaic Targum; Hebrew through me

units.leftText: If you are wise, you are wise for yourself. If you mock, you alone will bear it.
units.rightText: If you are wise, you are wise to your own advantage; but if you scoff, you alone will bear the consequences. The Way of Folly

units.leftText: The foolish woman is loud, undisciplined, and knows nothing.
units.rightText: The woman named Folly is loud; she is naive and knows nothing.

units.leftText: She sits at the door of her house, on a seat in the high places of the city,
units.rightText: She sits at the door of her house, on a seat in the heights of the city,

units.leftText: to call to those who pass by, who go straight on their ways,
units.rightText: calling out to those who pass by, who make their paths straight.

units.leftText: “Whoever is simple, let him turn in here.” As for him who is void of understanding, she says to him,
units.rightText: “Whoever is simple, let him turn in here!” she says to him who lacks judgment.

units.leftText: “Stolen water is sweet. Food eaten in secret is pleasant.”
units.rightText: “Stolen water is sweet, and bread eaten in secret is tasty!”

units.leftText: But he doesn’t know that the departed spirits are there, that her guests are in the depths of Sheol.
units.rightText: But they do not know that the dead are there, that her guests are in the depths of Sheol.
leftNotes: 9:18 Sheol is the place of the dead.
rightNotes: 9:18 Hebrew the Rephaim

units.leftText: The proverbs of Solomon. A wise son makes a glad father; but a foolish son brings grief to his mother.
units.rightText: The proverbs of Solomon: A wise son brings joy to his father, but a foolish son grief to his mother.

units.leftText: Treasures of wickedness profit nothing, but righteousness delivers from death.
units.rightText: Ill-gotten treasures profit nothing, but righteousness brings deliverance from death.

units.leftText: The LORD will not allow the soul of the righteous to go hungry, but he thrusts away the desire of the wicked.
units.rightText: The LORD does not let the righteous go hungry, but He denies the craving of the wicked.

units.leftText: He becomes poor who works with a lazy hand, but the hand of the diligent brings wealth.
units.rightText: Idle hands make one poor, but diligent hands bring wealth.

units.leftText: He who gathers in summer is a wise son, but he who sleeps during the harvest is a son who causes shame.
units.rightText: He who gathers in summer is a wise son, but he who sleeps during harvest is a disgraceful son.

units.leftText: Blessings are on the head of the righteous, but violence covers the mouth of the wicked.
units.rightText: Blessings are on the head of the righteous, but the mouth of the wicked conceals violence.
rightNotes: 10:6 Or but violence covers the mouth of the wicked; also in verse 11

units.leftText: The memory of the righteous is blessed, but the name of the wicked will rot.
units.rightText: The memory of the righteous is a blessing, but the name of the wicked will rot.

units.leftText: The wise in heart accept commandments, but a chattering fool will fall.
units.rightText: A wise heart will receive commandments, but foolish lips will come to ruin.

units.leftText: He who walks blamelessly walks surely, but he who perverts his ways will be found out.
units.rightText: He who walks in integrity walks securely, but he who perverts his ways will be found out.

units.leftText: One who winks with the eye causes sorrow, but a chattering fool will fall.
units.rightText: He who winks the eye causes grief, and foolish lips will come to ruin.
rightNotes: 10:10 Or babbling fools will fall

units.leftText: The mouth of the righteous is a spring of life, but violence covers the mouth of the wicked.
units.rightText: The mouth of the righteous is a fountain of life, but the mouth of the wicked conceals violence.

units.leftText: Hatred stirs up strife, but love covers all wrongs.
units.rightText: Hatred stirs up dissension, but love covers all transgressions.
rightNotes: 10:12 See 1 Peter 4:8|1PE 4:8*

units.leftText: Wisdom is found on the lips of him who has discernment, but a rod is for the back of him who is void of understanding.
units.rightText: Wisdom is found on the lips of the discerning, but a rod is for the back of him who lacks judgment.

units.leftText: Wise men lay up knowledge, but the mouth of the foolish is near ruin.
units.rightText: The wise store up knowledge, but the mouth of the fool invites destruction.

units.leftText: The rich man’s wealth is his strong city. The destruction of the poor is their poverty.
units.rightText: The wealth of the rich man is his fortified city, but poverty is the ruin of the poor.

units.leftText: The labor of the righteous leads to life. The increase of the wicked leads to sin.
units.rightText: The labor of the righteous leads to life, but the gain of the wicked brings punishment.

units.leftText: He is in the way of life who heeds correction, but he who forsakes reproof leads others astray.
units.rightText: Whoever heeds instruction is on the path to life, but he who ignores reproof goes astray.

units.leftText: He who hides hatred has lying lips. He who utters a slander is a fool.
units.rightText: The one who conceals hatred has lying lips, and whoever spreads slander is a fool.

units.leftText: In the multitude of words there is no lack of disobedience, but he who restrains his lips does wisely.
units.rightText: When words are many, sin is unavoidable, but he who restrains his lips is wise.

units.leftText: The tongue of the righteous is like choice silver. The heart of the wicked is of little worth.
units.rightText: The tongue of the righteous is choice silver, but the heart of the wicked has little worth.

units.leftText: The lips of the righteous feed many, but the foolish die for lack of understanding.
units.rightText: The lips of the righteous feed many, but fools die for lack of judgment.

units.leftText: The LORD’s blessing brings wealth, and he adds no trouble to it.
units.rightText: The blessing of the LORD enriches, and He adds no sorrow to it.

units.leftText: It is a fool’s pleasure to do wickedness, but wisdom is a man of understanding’s pleasure.
units.rightText: The fool delights in shameful conduct, but a man of understanding has wisdom.

units.leftText: What the wicked fear will overtake them, but the desire of the righteous will be granted.
units.rightText: What the wicked man dreads will overtake him, but the desire of the righteous will be granted.

units.leftText: When the whirlwind passes, the wicked is no more; but the righteous stand firm forever.
units.rightText: When the whirlwind passes, the wicked are no more, but the righteous are secure forever.

units.leftText: As vinegar to the teeth, and as smoke to the eyes, so is the sluggard to those who send him.
units.rightText: Like vinegar to the teeth and smoke to the eyes, so is the slacker to those who send him.

units.leftText: The fear of the LORD prolongs days, but the years of the wicked shall be shortened.
units.rightText: The fear of the LORD prolongs life, but the years of the wicked will be cut short.

units.leftText: The prospect of the righteous is joy, but the hope of the wicked will perish.
units.rightText: The hope of the righteous is joy, but the expectations of the wicked will perish.

units.leftText: The way of the LORD is a stronghold to the upright, but it is a destruction to the workers of iniquity.
units.rightText: The way of the LORD is a refuge to the upright, but destruction awaits those who do evil.

units.leftText: The righteous will never be removed, but the wicked will not dwell in the land.
units.rightText: The righteous will never be shaken, but the wicked will not inhabit the land.

units.leftText: The mouth of the righteous produces wisdom, but the perverse tongue will be cut off.
units.rightText: The mouth of the righteous brings forth wisdom, but a perverse tongue will be cut out.

units.leftText: The lips of the righteous know what is acceptable, but the mouth of the wicked is perverse.
units.rightText: The lips of the righteous know what is fitting, but the mouth of the wicked is perverse.

units.leftText: A false balance is an abomination to the LORD, but accurate weights are his delight.
units.rightText: Dishonest scales are an abomination to the LORD, but an accurate weight is His delight.

units.leftText: When pride comes, then comes shame, but with humility comes wisdom.
units.rightText: When pride comes, disgrace follows, but with humility comes wisdom.

units.leftText: The integrity of the upright shall guide them, but the perverseness of the treacherous shall destroy them.
units.rightText: The integrity of the upright guides them, but the perversity of the faithless destroys them.

units.leftText: Riches don’t profit in the day of wrath, but righteousness delivers from death.
units.rightText: Riches are worthless in the day of wrath, but righteousness brings deliverance from death.

units.leftText: The righteousness of the blameless will direct his way, but the wicked shall fall by his own wickedness.
units.rightText: The righteousness of the blameless directs their path, but the wicked fall by their own wickedness.

units.leftText: The righteousness of the upright shall deliver them, but the unfaithful will be trapped by evil desires.
units.rightText: The righteousness of the upright delivers them, but the faithless are trapped by their own desires.

units.leftText: When a wicked man dies, hope perishes, and expectation of power comes to nothing.
units.rightText: When the wicked man dies, his hope perishes, and the hope of his strength vanishes.

units.leftText: A righteous person is delivered out of trouble, and the wicked takes his place.
units.rightText: The righteous man is delivered from trouble; in his place the wicked man goes in.

units.leftText: With his mouth the godless man destroys his neighbor, but the righteous will be delivered through knowledge.
units.rightText: With his mouth the ungodly man destroys his neighbor, but through knowledge the righteous are rescued.

units.leftText: When it goes well with the righteous, the city rejoices. When the wicked perish, there is shouting.
units.rightText: When the righteous thrive, the city rejoices, and when the wicked perish, there are shouts of joy.

units.leftText: By the blessing of the upright, the city is exalted, but it is overthrown by the mouth of the wicked.
units.rightText: By the blessing of the upright a city is built up, but by the mouth of the wicked it is torn down.

units.leftText: One who despises his neighbor is void of wisdom, but a man of understanding holds his peace.
units.rightText: Whoever shows contempt for his neighbor lacks judgment, but a man of understanding remains silent.

units.leftText: One who brings gossip betrays a confidence, but one who is of a trustworthy spirit is one who keeps a secret.
units.rightText: A gossip reveals a secret, but a trustworthy person keeps a confidence.

units.leftText: Where there is no wise guidance, the nation falls, but in the multitude of counselors there is victory.
units.rightText: For lack of guidance, a nation falls, but with many counselors comes deliverance.

units.leftText: He who is collateral for a stranger will suffer for it, but he who refuses pledges of collateral is secure.
units.rightText: He who puts up security for a stranger will surely suffer, but the one who hates indebtedness is secure.

units.leftText: A gracious woman obtains honor, but violent men obtain riches.
units.rightText: A gracious woman attains honor, but ruthless men gain only wealth.

units.leftText: The merciful man does good to his own soul, but he who is cruel troubles his own flesh.
units.rightText: A kind man benefits himself, but a cruel man brings trouble on himself.

units.leftText: Wicked people earn deceitful wages, but one who sows righteousness reaps a sure reward.
units.rightText: The wicked man earns an empty wage, but he who sows righteousness reaps a true reward.

units.leftText: He who is truly righteous gets life. He who pursues evil gets death.
units.rightText: Genuine righteousness leads to life, but the pursuit of evil brings death.

units.leftText: Those who are perverse in heart are an abomination to the LORD, but those whose ways are blameless are his delight.
units.rightText: The perverse in heart are an abomination to the LORD, but the blameless in their walk are His delight.

units.leftText: Most certainly, the evil man will not be unpunished, but the offspring of the righteous will be delivered.
units.rightText: Be assured that the wicked will not go unpunished, but the offspring of the righteous will escape.

units.leftText: Like a gold ring in a pig’s snout, is a beautiful woman who lacks discretion.
units.rightText: Like a gold ring in a pig’s snout is a beautiful woman who lacks discretion.

units.leftText: The desire of the righteous is only good. The expectation of the wicked is wrath.
units.rightText: The desire of the righteous leads only to good, but the hope of the wicked brings wrath.

units.leftText: There is one who scatters, and increases yet more. There is one who withholds more than is appropriate, but gains poverty.
units.rightText: One gives freely, yet gains even more; another withholds what is right, only to become poor.

units.leftText: The liberal soul shall be made fat. He who waters shall be watered also himself.
units.rightText: A generous soul will prosper, and he who refreshes others will himself be refreshed.

units.leftText: People curse someone who withholds grain, but blessing will be on the head of him who sells it.
units.rightText: The people will curse the hoarder of grain, but blessing will crown the one who sells it.

units.leftText: He who diligently seeks good seeks favor, but he who searches after evil, it shall come to him.
units.rightText: He who searches out good finds favor, but evil will come to him who seeks it.

units.leftText: He who trusts in his riches will fall, but the righteous shall flourish as the green leaf.
units.rightText: He who trusts in his riches will fall, but the righteous will thrive like foliage.

units.leftText: He who troubles his own house shall inherit the wind. The foolish shall be servant to the wise of heart.
units.rightText: He who brings trouble on his house will inherit the wind, and the fool will be servant to the wise of heart.

units.leftText: The fruit of the righteous is a tree of life. He who is wise wins souls.
units.rightText: The fruit of the righteous is a tree of life, and he who wins souls is wise.

units.leftText: Behold, the righteous shall be repaid on the earth, how much more the wicked and the sinner!
units.rightText: If the righteous receive their due on earth, how much more the ungodly and the sinner!
rightNotes: 11:31 LXX If it is hard for the righteous to be saved, what will become of the ungodly and the sinner?Cited in 1 Peter 4:18|1PE 4:18*

units.leftText: Whoever loves correction loves knowledge, but he who hates reproof is stupid.
units.rightText: Whoever loves discipline loves knowledge, but he who hates correction is stupid.

units.leftText: A good man shall obtain favor from the LORD, but he will condemn a man of wicked plans.
units.rightText: The good man obtains favor from the LORD, but the LORD condemns a man who devises evil.

units.leftText: A man shall not be established by wickedness, but the root of the righteous shall not be moved.
units.rightText: A man cannot be established through wickedness, but the righteous cannot be uprooted.

units.leftText: A worthy woman is the crown of her husband, but a disgraceful wife is as rottenness in his bones.
units.rightText: A wife of noble character is her husband’s crown, but she who causes shame is like decay in his bones.

units.leftText: The thoughts of the righteous are just, but the advice of the wicked is deceitful.
units.rightText: The plans of the righteous are just, but the counsel of the wicked leads to deceit.

units.leftText: The words of the wicked are about lying in wait for blood, but the speech of the upright rescues them.
units.rightText: The words of the wicked lie in wait for blood, but the speech of the upright rescues them.

units.leftText: The wicked are overthrown, and are no more, but the house of the righteous shall stand.
units.rightText: The wicked are overthrown and perish, but the house of the righteous will stand.

units.leftText: A man shall be commended according to his wisdom, but he who has a warped mind shall be despised.
units.rightText: A man is praised according to his wisdom, but a twisted mind is despised.

units.leftText: Better is he who is little known, and has a servant, than he who honors himself and lacks bread.
units.rightText: Better to be lightly esteemed yet have a servant, than to be self-important but lack food.

units.leftText: A righteous man respects the life of his animal, but the tender mercies of the wicked are cruel.
units.rightText: A righteous man regards the life of his animal, but the tender mercies of the wicked are only cruelty.

units.leftText: He who tills his land shall have plenty of bread, but he who chases fantasies is void of understanding.
units.rightText: The one who works his land will have plenty of food, but whoever chases fantasies lacks judgment.

units.leftText: The wicked desires the plunder of evil men, but the root of the righteous flourishes.
units.rightText: The wicked desire the plunder of evil men, but the root of the righteous flourishes.

units.leftText: An evil man is trapped by sinfulness of lips, but the righteous shall come out of trouble.
units.rightText: An evil man is trapped by his rebellious speech, but a righteous man escapes from trouble.

units.leftText: A man shall be satisfied with good by the fruit of his mouth. The work of a man’s hands shall be rewarded to him.
units.rightText: By fruitful speech a man is filled with good things, and the work of his hands returns to him.

units.leftText: The way of a fool is right in his own eyes, but he who is wise listens to counsel.
units.rightText: The way of a fool is right in his own eyes, but a wise man listens to counsel.

units.leftText: A fool shows his annoyance the same day, but one who overlooks an insult is prudent.
units.rightText: A fool’s anger is known at once, but a prudent man overlooks an insult.

units.leftText: He who is truthful testifies honestly, but a false witness lies.
units.rightText: He who speaks the truth declares what is right, but a false witness speaks deceit.

units.leftText: There is one who speaks rashly like the piercing of a sword, but the tongue of the wise heals.
units.rightText: Speaking rashly is like a piercing sword, but the tongue of the wise brings healing.

units.leftText: Truth’s lips will be established forever, but a lying tongue is only momentary.
units.rightText: Truthful lips endure forever, but a lying tongue lasts only a moment.

units.leftText: Deceit is in the heart of those who plot evil, but joy comes to the promoters of peace.
units.rightText: Deceit is in the hearts of those who devise evil, but the counselors of peace have joy.

units.leftText: No mischief shall happen to the righteous, but the wicked shall be filled with evil.
units.rightText: No harm befalls the righteous, but the wicked are filled with trouble.

units.leftText: Lying lips are an abomination to the LORD, but those who do the truth are his delight.
units.rightText: Lying lips are detestable to the LORD, but those who deal faithfully are His delight.

units.leftText: A prudent man keeps his knowledge, but the hearts of fools proclaim foolishness.
units.rightText: A shrewd man keeps his knowledge to himself, but a foolish heart proclaims its folly.

units.leftText: The hands of the diligent ones shall rule, but laziness ends in slave labor.
units.rightText: The hand of the diligent will rule, but laziness ends in forced labor.

units.leftText: Anxiety in a man’s heart weighs it down, but a kind word makes it glad.
units.rightText: Anxiety weighs down the heart of a man, but a good word cheers it up.

units.leftText: A righteous person is cautious in friendship, but the way of the wicked leads them astray.
units.rightText: A righteous man is cautious in friendship, but the ways of the wicked lead them astray.

units.leftText: The slothful man doesn’t roast his game, but the possessions of diligent men are prized.
units.rightText: A lazy man does not roast his game, but a diligent man prizes his possession.

units.leftText: In the way of righteousness is life; in its path there is no death.
units.rightText: There is life in the path of righteousness, but another path leads to death.

units.leftText: A wise son listens to his father’s instruction, but a scoffer doesn’t listen to rebuke.
units.rightText: A wise son heeds his father’s discipline, but a mocker does not listen to rebuke.

units.leftText: By the fruit of his lips, a man enjoys good things, but the unfaithful crave violence.
units.rightText: From the fruit of his lips a man enjoys good things, but the desire of the faithless is violence.

units.leftText: He who guards his mouth guards his soul. One who opens wide his lips comes to ruin.
units.rightText: He who guards his mouth protects his life, but the one who opens his lips invites his own ruin.

units.leftText: The soul of the sluggard desires, and has nothing, but the desire of the diligent shall be fully satisfied.
units.rightText: The slacker craves yet has nothing, but the soul of the diligent is fully satisfied.

units.leftText: A righteous man hates lies, but a wicked man brings shame and disgrace.
units.rightText: The righteous hate falsehood, but the wicked bring shame and disgrace.

units.leftText: Righteousness guards the way of integrity, but wickedness overthrows the sinner.
units.rightText: Righteousness guards the man of integrity, but wickedness undermines the sinner.

units.leftText: There are some who pretend to be rich, yet have nothing. There are some who pretend to be poor, yet have great wealth.
units.rightText: One pretends to be rich, but has nothing; another pretends to be poor, yet has great wealth.

units.leftText: The ransom of a man’s life is his riches, but the poor hear no threats.
units.rightText: Riches may ransom a man’s life, but a poor man hears no threat.

units.leftText: The light of the righteous shines brightly, but the lamp of the wicked is snuffed out.
units.rightText: The light of the righteous shines brightly, but the lamp of the wicked is extinguished.

units.leftText: Pride only breeds quarrels, but wisdom is with people who take advice.
units.rightText: Arrogance leads only to strife, but wisdom is with the well-advised.

units.leftText: Wealth gained dishonestly dwindles away, but he who gathers by hand makes it grow.
units.rightText: Dishonest wealth will dwindle, but what is earned through hard work will be multiplied.

units.leftText: Hope deferred makes the heart sick, but when longing is fulfilled, it is a tree of life.
units.rightText: Hope deferred makes the heart sick, but desire fulfilled is a tree of life.

units.leftText: Whoever despises instruction will pay for it, but he who respects a command will be rewarded.
units.rightText: He who despises instruction will pay the penalty, but the one who respects a command will be rewarded.

units.leftText: The teaching of the wise is a spring of life, to turn from the snares of death.
units.rightText: The teaching of the wise is a fountain of life, turning one from the snares of death.
rightNotes: 13:14 Or law

units.leftText: Good understanding wins favor, but the way of the unfaithful is hard.
units.rightText: Good understanding wins favor, but the way of the faithless is difficult.

units.leftText: Every prudent man acts from knowledge, but a fool exposes folly.
units.rightText: Every prudent man acts with knowledge, but a fool displays his folly.

units.leftText: A wicked messenger falls into trouble, but a trustworthy envoy gains healing.
units.rightText: A wicked messenger falls into trouble, but a faithful envoy brings healing.

units.leftText: Poverty and shame come to him who refuses discipline, but he who heeds correction shall be honored.
units.rightText: Poverty and shame come to him who ignores discipline, but whoever heeds correction is honored.

units.leftText: Longing fulfilled is sweet to the soul, but fools detest turning from evil.
units.rightText: Desire fulfilled is sweet to the soul, but turning from evil is detestable to fools.

units.leftText: One who walks with wise men grows wise, but a companion of fools suffers harm.
units.rightText: He who walks with the wise will become wise, but the companion of fools will be destroyed.

units.leftText: Misfortune pursues sinners, but prosperity rewards the righteous.
units.rightText: Disaster pursues sinners, but prosperity is the reward of the righteous.

units.leftText: A good man leaves an inheritance to his children’s children, but the wealth of the sinner is stored for the righteous.
units.rightText: A good man leaves an inheritance to his children’s children, but the sinner’s wealth is passed to the righteous.

units.leftText: An abundance of food is in poor people’s fields, but injustice sweeps it away.
units.rightText: Abundant food is in the fallow ground of the poor, but without justice it is swept away.

units.leftText: One who spares the rod hates his son, but one who loves him is careful to discipline him.
units.rightText: He who spares the rod hates his son, but he who loves him disciplines him diligently.

units.leftText: The righteous one eats to the satisfying of his soul, but the belly of the wicked goes hungry.
units.rightText: A righteous man eats to his heart’s content, but the stomach of the wicked is empty.

units.leftText: Every wise woman builds her house, but the foolish one tears it down with her own hands.
units.rightText: Every wise woman builds her house, but a foolish one tears it down with her own hands.

units.leftText: He who walks in his uprightness fears the LORD, but he who is perverse in his ways despises him.
units.rightText: He who walks in uprightness fears the LORD, but the one who is devious in his ways despises Him.

units.leftText: The fool’s talk brings a rod to his back, but the lips of the wise protect them.
units.rightText: The proud speech of a fool brings a rod to his back, but the lips of the wise protect them.

units.leftText: Where no oxen are, the crib is clean, but much increase is by the strength of the ox.
units.rightText: Where there are no oxen, the manger is empty, but an abundant harvest comes through the strength of the ox.

units.leftText: A truthful witness will not lie, but a false witness pours out lies.
units.rightText: An honest witness does not deceive, but a dishonest witness pours forth lies.

units.leftText: A scoffer seeks wisdom, and doesn’t find it, but knowledge comes easily to a discerning person.
units.rightText: A mocker seeks wisdom and finds none, but knowledge comes easily to the discerning.

units.leftText: Stay away from a foolish man, for you won’t find knowledge on his lips.
units.rightText: Stay away from a foolish man; you will gain no knowledge from his speech.

units.leftText: The wisdom of the prudent is to think about his way, but the folly of fools is deceit.
units.rightText: The wisdom of the prudent is to discern his way, but the folly of fools deceives them.

units.leftText: Fools mock at making atonement for sins, but among the upright there is good will.
units.rightText: Fools mock the making of amends, but goodwill is found among the upright.

units.leftText: The heart knows its own bitterness and joy; he will not share these with a stranger.
units.rightText: The heart knows its own bitterness, and no stranger shares in its joy.

units.leftText: The house of the wicked will be overthrown, but the tent of the upright will flourish.
units.rightText: The house of the wicked will be destroyed, but the tent of the upright will flourish.

units.leftText: There is a way which seems right to a man, but in the end it leads to death.
units.rightText: There is a way that seems right to a man, but its end is the way of death.

units.leftText: Even in laughter the heart may be sorrowful, and mirth may end in heaviness.
units.rightText: Even in laughter the heart may ache, and joy may end in sorrow.

units.leftText: The unfaithful will be repaid for his own ways; likewise a good man will be rewarded for his ways.
units.rightText: The backslider in heart receives the fill of his own ways, but a good man is rewarded for his ways.

units.leftText: A simple man believes everything, but the prudent man carefully considers his ways.
units.rightText: The simple man believes every word, but the prudent man watches his steps.

units.leftText: A wise man fears and shuns evil, but the fool is hot headed and reckless.
units.rightText: A wise man fears and turns from evil, but a fool is careless and reckless.
rightNotes: 14:16 Or fears the LORD

units.leftText: He who is quick to become angry will commit folly, and a crafty man is hated.
units.rightText: A quick-tempered man acts foolishly, and a devious man is hated.

units.leftText: The simple inherit folly, but the prudent are crowned with knowledge.
units.rightText: The simple inherit folly, but the prudent are crowned with knowledge.

units.leftText: The evil bow down before the good, and the wicked at the gates of the righteous.
units.rightText: The evil bow before the good, and the wicked at the gates of the righteous.

units.leftText: The poor person is shunned even by his own neighbor, but the rich person has many friends.
