units.rightText: The poor man is hated even by his neighbor, but many are those who love the rich.

units.leftText: He who despises his neighbor sins, but he who has pity on the poor is blessed.
units.rightText: He who despises his neighbor sins, but blessed is he who shows kindness to the poor.

units.leftText: Don’t they go astray who plot evil? But love and faithfulness belong to those who plan good.
units.rightText: Do not those who contrive evil go astray? But those who plan goodness find loving devotion and faithfulness.
rightNotes: 14:22 Or show

units.leftText: In all hard work there is profit, but the talk of the lips leads only to poverty.
units.rightText: There is profit in all labor, but mere talk leads only to poverty.

units.leftText: The crown of the wise is their riches, but the folly of fools crowns them with folly.
units.rightText: The crown of the wise is their wealth, but the effort of fools is folly.

units.leftText: A truthful witness saves souls, but a false witness is deceitful.
units.rightText: A truthful witness saves lives, but one who utters lies is deceitful.

units.leftText: In the fear of the LORD is a secure fortress, and he will be a refuge for his children.
units.rightText: He who fears the LORD is secure in confidence, and his children shall have a place of refuge.

units.leftText: The fear of the LORD is a fountain of life, turning people from the snares of death.
units.rightText: The fear of the LORD is a fountain of life, turning a man from the snares of death.

units.leftText: In the multitude of people is the king’s glory, but in the lack of people is the destruction of the prince.
units.rightText: A large population is a king’s splendor, but a lack of subjects is a prince’s ruin.

units.leftText: He who is slow to anger has great understanding, but he who has a quick temper displays folly.
units.rightText: A patient man has great understanding, but a quick-tempered man promotes folly.

units.leftText: The life of the body is a heart at peace, but envy rots the bones.
units.rightText: A tranquil heart is life to the body, but envy rots the bones.

units.leftText: He who oppresses the poor shows contempt for his Maker, but he who is kind to the needy honors him.
units.rightText: Whoever oppresses the poor taunts their Maker, but whoever is kind to the needy honors Him.

units.leftText: The wicked is brought down in his calamity, but in death, the righteous has a refuge.
units.rightText: The wicked man is thrown down by his own sin, but the righteous man has a refuge even in death.

units.leftText: Wisdom rests in the heart of one who has understanding, and is even made known in the inward part of fools.
units.rightText: Wisdom rests in the heart of the discerning; even among fools she is known.
rightNotes: 14:33 Hebrew; LXX and Syriac but among fools she is not known

units.leftText: Righteousness exalts a nation, but sin is a disgrace to any people.
units.rightText: Righteousness exalts a nation, but sin is a disgrace to any people.

units.leftText: The king’s favor is toward a servant who deals wisely, but his wrath is toward one who causes shame.
units.rightText: A king delights in a wise servant, but his anger falls on the shameful.

units.leftText: A gentle answer turns away wrath, but a harsh word stirs up anger.
units.rightText: A gentle answer turns away wrath, but a harsh word stirs up anger.

units.leftText: The tongue of the wise commends knowledge, but the mouths of fools gush out folly.
units.rightText: The tongue of the wise commends knowledge, but the mouth of the fool spouts folly.

units.leftText: The LORD’s eyes are everywhere, keeping watch on the evil and the good.
units.rightText: The eyes of the LORD are in every place, observing the evil and the good.

units.leftText: A gentle tongue is a tree of life, but deceit in it crushes the spirit.
units.rightText: A soothing tongue is a tree of life, but a perverse tongue crushes the spirit.

units.leftText: A fool despises his father’s correction, but he who heeds reproof shows prudence.
units.rightText: A fool rejects his father’s discipline, but whoever heeds correction is prudent.

units.leftText: In the house of the righteous is much treasure, but the income of the wicked brings trouble.
units.rightText: The house of the righteous has great treasure, but the income of the wicked is trouble.

units.leftText: The lips of the wise spread knowledge; not so with the heart of fools.
units.rightText: The lips of the wise spread knowledge, but not so the hearts of fools.

units.leftText: The sacrifice made by the wicked is an abomination to the LORD, but the prayer of the upright is his delight.
units.rightText: The sacrifice of the wicked is detestable to the LORD, but the prayer of the upright is His delight.

units.leftText: The way of the wicked is an abomination to the LORD, but he loves him who follows after righteousness.
units.rightText: The LORD detests the way of the wicked, but He loves those who pursue righteousness.

units.leftText: There is stern discipline for one who forsakes the way. Whoever hates reproof shall die.
units.rightText: Discipline is harsh for him who leaves the path; he who hates correction will die.

units.leftText: Sheol and Abaddon are before the LORD— how much more then the hearts of the children of men!
units.rightText: Sheol and Abaddon lie open before the LORD— how much more the hearts of men!
leftNotes: 15:11 Sheol is the place of the dead.
rightNotes: 15:11 Or Death and Destruction

units.leftText: A scoffer doesn’t love to be reproved; he will not go to the wise.
units.rightText: A mocker does not love to be reproved, nor will he consult the wise.

units.leftText: A glad heart makes a cheerful face, but an aching heart breaks the spirit.
units.rightText: A joyful heart makes a cheerful countenance, but sorrow of the heart crushes the spirit.

units.leftText: The heart of one who has understanding seeks knowledge, but the mouths of fools feed on folly.
units.rightText: A discerning heart seeks knowledge, but the mouth of a fool feeds on folly.

units.leftText: All the days of the afflicted are wretched, but one who has a cheerful heart enjoys a continual feast.
units.rightText: All the days of the oppressed are bad, but a cheerful heart has a continual feast.

units.leftText: Better is little, with the fear of the LORD, than great treasure with trouble.
units.rightText: Better a little with the fear of the LORD than great treasure with turmoil.

units.leftText: Better is a dinner of herbs, where love is, than a fattened calf with hatred.
units.rightText: Better a dish of vegetables where there is love than a fattened ox with hatred.

units.leftText: A wrathful man stirs up contention, but one who is slow to anger appeases strife.
units.rightText: A hot-tempered man stirs up strife, but he who is slow to anger calms dispute.

units.leftText: The way of the sluggard is like a thorn patch, but the path of the upright is a highway.
units.rightText: The way of the slacker is like a hedge of thorns, but the path of the upright is a highway.

units.leftText: A wise son makes a father glad, but a foolish man despises his mother.
units.rightText: A wise son brings joy to his father, but a foolish man despises his mother.

units.leftText: Folly is joy to one who is void of wisdom, but a man of understanding keeps his way straight.
units.rightText: Folly is joy to one who lacks judgment, but a man of understanding walks a straight path.

units.leftText: Where there is no counsel, plans fail; but in a multitude of counselors they are established.
units.rightText: Plans fail for lack of counsel, but with many advisers they succeed.

units.leftText: Joy comes to a man with the reply of his mouth. How good is a word at the right time!
units.rightText: A man takes joy in a fitting reply — and how good is a timely word!

units.leftText: The path of life leads upward for the wise, to keep him from going downward to Sheol.
units.rightText: The path of life leads upward for the wise, that he may avoid going down to Sheol.
leftNotes: 15:24 Sheol is the place of the dead.

units.leftText: The LORD will uproot the house of the proud, but he will keep the widow’s borders intact.
units.rightText: The LORD tears down the house of the proud, but He protects the boundaries of the widow.

units.leftText: The LORD detests the thoughts of the wicked, but the thoughts of the pure are pleasing.
units.rightText: The LORD detests the thoughts of the wicked, but the words of the pure are pleasant to Him.

units.leftText: He who is greedy for gain troubles his own house, but he who hates bribes will live.
units.rightText: He who is greedy for unjust gain brings trouble on his household, but he who hates bribes will live.

units.leftText: The heart of the righteous weighs answers, but the mouth of the wicked gushes out evil.
units.rightText: The heart of the righteous ponders how to answer, but the mouth of the wicked blurts out evil.

units.leftText: The LORD is far from the wicked, but he hears the prayer of the righteous.
units.rightText: The LORD is far from the wicked, but He hears the prayer of the righteous.

units.leftText: The light of the eyes rejoices the heart. Good news gives health to the bones.
units.rightText: The light of the eyes cheers the heart, and good news nourishes the bones.

units.leftText: The ear that listens to reproof lives, and will be at home among the wise.
units.rightText: He who listens to life-giving reproof will dwell among the wise.

units.leftText: He who refuses correction despises his own soul, but he who listens to reproof gets understanding.
units.rightText: He who ignores discipline despises himself, but whoever heeds correction gains understanding.

units.leftText: The fear of the LORD teaches wisdom. Before honor is humility.
units.rightText: The fear of the LORD is the instruction of wisdom, and humility comes before honor.

units.leftText: The plans of the heart belong to man, but the answer of the tongue is from the LORD.
units.rightText: The plans of the heart belong to man, but the reply of the tongue is from the LORD.

units.leftText: All the ways of a man are clean in his own eyes, but the LORD weighs the motives.
units.rightText: All a man’s ways are pure in his own eyes, but his motives are weighed out by the LORD.

units.leftText: Commit your deeds to the LORD, and your plans shall succeed.
units.rightText: Commit your works to the LORD and your plans will be achieved.

units.leftText: The LORD has made everything for its own end— yes, even the wicked for the day of evil.
units.rightText: The LORD has made everything for His purpose— even the wicked for the day of disaster.

units.leftText: Everyone who is proud in heart is an abomination to the LORD; they shall certainly not be unpunished.
units.rightText: Everyone who is proud in heart is detestable to the LORD; be assured that he will not go unpunished.

units.leftText: By mercy and truth iniquity is atoned for. By the fear of the LORD men depart from evil.
units.rightText: By loving devotion and faithfulness iniquity is atoned for, and by the fear of the LORD one turns aside from evil.

units.leftText: When a man’s ways please the LORD, he makes even his enemies to be at peace with him.
units.rightText: When a man’s ways please the LORD, He makes even the man’s enemies live at peace with him.

units.leftText: Better is a little with righteousness, than great revenues with injustice.
units.rightText: Better a little with righteousness than great gain with injustice.

units.leftText: A man’s heart plans his course, but the LORD directs his steps.
units.rightText: A man’s heart plans his course, but the LORD determines his steps.

units.leftText: Inspired judgments are on the lips of the king. He shall not betray his mouth.
units.rightText: A divine verdict is on the lips of a king; his mouth must not betray justice.

units.leftText: Honest balances and scales are the LORD’s; all the weights in the bag are his work.
units.rightText: Honest scales and balances are from the LORD; all the weights in the bag are His concern.

units.leftText: It is an abomination for kings to do wrong, for the throne is established by righteousness.
units.rightText: Wicked behavior is detestable for kings, for a throne is established through righteousness.

units.leftText: Righteous lips are the delight of kings. They value one who speaks the truth.
units.rightText: Righteous lips are a king’s delight, and he who speaks honestly is beloved.

units.leftText: The king’s wrath is a messenger of death, but a wise man will pacify it.
units.rightText: The wrath of a king is a messenger of death, but a wise man will pacify it.

units.leftText: In the light of the king’s face is life. His favor is like a cloud of the spring rain.
units.rightText: When a king’s face brightens, there is life; his favor is like a rain cloud in spring.

units.leftText: How much better it is to get wisdom than gold! Yes, to get understanding is to be chosen rather than silver.
units.rightText: How much better to acquire wisdom than gold! To gain understanding is more desirable than silver.

units.leftText: The highway of the upright is to depart from evil. He who keeps his way preserves his soul.
units.rightText: The highway of the upright leads away from evil; he who guards his way protects his life.

units.leftText: Pride goes before destruction, and an arrogant spirit before a fall.
units.rightText: Pride goes before destruction, and a haughty spirit before a fall.

units.leftText: It is better to be of a lowly spirit with the poor, than to divide the plunder with the proud.
units.rightText: It is better to be lowly in spirit among the humble than to divide the spoil with the proud.

units.leftText: He who heeds the Word finds prosperity. Whoever trusts in the LORD is blessed.
units.rightText: Whoever heeds instruction will find success, and blessed is he who trusts in the LORD.
rightNotes: 16:20 Or Whoever speaks prudently will find what is good

units.leftText: The wise in heart shall be called prudent. Pleasantness of the lips promotes instruction.
units.rightText: The wise in heart are called discerning, and pleasant speech promotes instruction.

units.leftText: Understanding is a fountain of life to one who has it, but the punishment of fools is their folly.
units.rightText: Understanding is a fountain of life to its possessor, but the discipline of fools is folly.

units.leftText: The heart of the wise instructs his mouth, and adds learning to his lips.
units.rightText: The heart of the wise man instructs his mouth and adds persuasiveness to his lips.

units.leftText: Pleasant words are a honeycomb, sweet to the soul, and health to the bones.
units.rightText: Pleasant words are a honeycomb, sweet to the soul and healing to the bones.

units.leftText: There is a way which seems right to a man, but in the end it leads to death.
units.rightText: There is a way that seems right to a man, but its end is the way of death.

units.leftText: The appetite of the laboring man labors for him, for his mouth urges him on.
units.rightText: A worker’s appetite works for him because his hunger drives him onward.

units.leftText: A worthless man devises mischief. His speech is like a scorching fire.
units.rightText: A worthless man digs up evil, and his speech is like a scorching fire.
rightNotes: 16:27 Or and what is on his lips

units.leftText: A perverse man stirs up strife. A whisperer separates close friends.
units.rightText: A perverse man spreads dissension, and a gossip divides close friends.

units.leftText: A man of violence entices his neighbor, and leads him in a way that is not good.
units.rightText: A violent man entices his neighbor and leads him down a path that is not good.

units.leftText: One who winks his eyes to plot perversities, one who compresses his lips, is bent on evil.
units.rightText: He who winks his eye devises perversity; he who purses his lips is bent on evil.

units.leftText: Gray hair is a crown of glory. It is attained by a life of righteousness.
units.rightText: Gray hair is a crown of glory; it is attained along the path of righteousness.

units.leftText: One who is slow to anger is better than the mighty; one who rules his spirit, than he who takes a city.
units.rightText: He who is slow to anger is better than a warrior, and he who controls his temper is greater than one who captures a city.

units.leftText: The lot is cast into the lap, but its every decision is from the LORD.
units.rightText: The lot is cast into the lap, but its every decision is from the LORD.

units.leftText: Better is a dry morsel with quietness, than a house full of feasting with strife.
units.rightText: Better a dry morsel in quietness than a house full of feasting with strife.
rightNotes: 17:1 Or sacrifices

units.leftText: A servant who deals wisely will rule over a son who causes shame, and shall have a part in the inheritance among the brothers.
units.rightText: A wise servant will rule over a disgraceful son and share his inheritance as one of the brothers.

units.leftText: The refining pot is for silver, and the furnace for gold, but the LORD tests the hearts.
units.rightText: A crucible for silver and a furnace for gold, but the LORD is the tester of hearts.

units.leftText: An evildoer heeds wicked lips. A liar gives ear to a mischievous tongue.
units.rightText: A wicked man listens to evil lips; a liar gives ear to a destructive tongue.

units.leftText: Whoever mocks the poor reproaches his Maker. He who is glad at calamity shall not be unpunished.
units.rightText: He who mocks the poor insults their Maker; whoever gloats over calamity will not go unpunished.

units.leftText: Children’s children are the crown of old men; the glory of children is their parents.
units.rightText: Grandchildren are the crown of the aged, and the glory of a son is his father.

units.leftText: Excellent speech isn’t fitting for a fool, much less do lying lips fit a prince.
units.rightText: Eloquent words are unfit for a fool; how much worse are lying lips to a ruler!

units.leftText: A bribe is a precious stone in the eyes of him who gives it; wherever he turns, he prospers.
units.rightText: A bribe is a charm to its giver; wherever he turns, he succeeds.

units.leftText: He who covers an offense promotes love; but he who repeats a matter separates best friends.
units.rightText: Whoever conceals an offense promotes love, but he who brings it up separates friends.

units.leftText: A rebuke enters deeper into one who has understanding than a hundred lashes into a fool.
units.rightText: A rebuke cuts into a man of discernment deeper than a hundred lashes cut into a fool.

units.leftText: An evil man seeks only rebellion; therefore a cruel messenger shall be sent against him.
units.rightText: An evil man seeks only rebellion; a cruel messenger will be sent against him.

units.leftText: Let a bear robbed of her cubs meet a man, rather than a fool in his folly.
units.rightText: It is better to meet a bear robbed of her cubs than a fool in his folly.

units.leftText: Whoever rewards evil for good, evil shall not depart from his house.
units.rightText: If anyone returns evil for good, evil will never leave his house.

units.leftText: The beginning of strife is like breaching a dam, therefore stop contention before quarreling breaks out.
units.rightText: To start a quarrel is to release a flood; so abandon the dispute before it breaks out.

units.leftText: He who justifies the wicked, and he who condemns the righteous, both of them alike are an abomination to the LORD.
units.rightText: Acquitting the guilty and condemning the righteous— both are detestable to the LORD.

units.leftText: Why is there money in the hand of a fool to buy wisdom, since he has no understanding?
units.rightText: Why should the fool have money in his hand with no intention of buying wisdom?

units.leftText: A friend loves at all times; and a brother is born for adversity.
units.rightText: A friend loves at all times, and a brother is born for adversity.

units.leftText: A man void of understanding strikes hands, and becomes collateral in the presence of his neighbor.
units.rightText: A man lacking judgment strikes hands in pledge and puts up security for his neighbor.

units.leftText: He who loves disobedience loves strife. One who builds a high gate seeks destruction.
units.rightText: He who loves transgression loves strife; he who builds his gate high invites destruction.

units.leftText: One who has a perverse heart doesn’t find prosperity, and one who has a deceitful tongue falls into trouble.
units.rightText: The one with a perverse heart finds no good, and he whose tongue is deceitful falls into trouble.

units.leftText: He who becomes the father of a fool grieves. The father of a fool has no joy.
units.rightText: A man fathers a fool to his own grief; the father of a fool has no joy.

units.leftText: A cheerful heart makes good medicine, but a crushed spirit dries up the bones.
units.rightText: A joyful heart is good medicine, but a broken spirit dries up the bones.

units.leftText: A wicked man receives a bribe in secret, to pervert the ways of justice.
units.rightText: A wicked man takes a covert bribe to subvert the course of justice.
rightNotes: 17:23 Hebrew a bribe from the bosom

units.leftText: Wisdom is before the face of one who has understanding, but the eyes of a fool wander to the ends of the earth.
units.rightText: Wisdom is the focus of the discerning, but the eyes of a fool wander to the ends of the earth.

units.leftText: A foolish son brings grief to his father, and bitterness to her who bore him.
units.rightText: A foolish son brings grief to his father and bitterness to her who bore him.

units.leftText: Also to punish the righteous is not good, nor to flog officials for their integrity.
units.rightText: It is surely not good to punish the innocent or to flog a noble for his honesty.

units.leftText: He who spares his words has knowledge. He who is even tempered is a man of understanding.
units.rightText: A man of knowledge restrains his words, and a man of understanding maintains a calm spirit.

units.leftText: Even a fool, when he keeps silent, is counted wise. When he shuts his lips, he is thought to be discerning.
units.rightText: Even a fool is considered wise if he keeps silent, and discerning when he holds his tongue.

units.leftText: A man who isolates himself pursues selfishness, and defies all sound judgment.
units.rightText: He who isolates himself pursues selfish desires; he rebels against all sound judgment.

units.leftText: A fool has no delight in understanding, but only in revealing his own opinion.
units.rightText: A fool does not delight in understanding, but only in airing his opinions.

units.leftText: When wickedness comes, contempt also comes, and with shame comes disgrace.
units.rightText: With a wicked man comes contempt as well, and shame is accompanied by disgrace.

units.leftText: The words of a man’s mouth are like deep waters. The fountain of wisdom is like a flowing brook.
units.rightText: The words of a man’s mouth are deep waters; the fountain of wisdom is a bubbling brook.

units.leftText: To be partial to the faces of the wicked is not good, nor to deprive the innocent of justice.
units.rightText: Showing partiality to the wicked is not good, nor is depriving the innocent of justice.
rightNotes: 18:5 Hebrew Lifting the face

units.leftText: A fool’s lips come into strife, and his mouth invites beatings.
units.rightText: A fool’s lips bring him strife, and his mouth invites a beating.

units.leftText: A fool’s mouth is his destruction, and his lips are a snare to his soul.
units.rightText: A fool’s mouth is his ruin, and his lips are a snare to his soul.

units.leftText: The words of a gossip are like dainty morsels: they go down into a person’s innermost parts.
units.rightText: The words of a gossip are like choice morsels that go down into the inmost being.

units.leftText: One who is slack in his work is brother to him who is a master of destruction.
units.rightText: Whoever is slothful in his work is brother to him who destroys.

units.leftText: The LORD’s name is a strong tower: the righteous run to him, and are safe.
units.rightText: The name of the LORD is a strong tower; the righteous run to it and are safe.
rightNotes: 18:10 Or to Him

units.leftText: The rich man’s wealth is his strong city, like an unscalable wall in his own imagination.
units.rightText: A rich man’s wealth is his fortified city; it is like a high wall in his imagination.

units.leftText: Before destruction the heart of man is proud, but before honor is humility.
units.rightText: Before his downfall a man’s heart is proud, but humility comes before honor.

units.leftText: He who answers before he hears, that is folly and shame to him.
units.rightText: He who answers a matter before he hears it— this is folly and disgrace to him.

units.leftText: A man’s spirit will sustain him in sickness, but a crushed spirit, who can bear?
units.rightText: The spirit of a man can endure his sickness, but who can survive a broken spirit?

units.leftText: The heart of the discerning gets knowledge. The ear of the wise seeks knowledge.
units.rightText: The heart of the discerning acquires knowledge, and the ear of the wise seeks it out.

units.leftText: A man’s gift makes room for him, and brings him before great men.
units.rightText: A man’s gift opens doors for him, and brings him before great men.

units.leftText: He who pleads his cause first seems right— until another comes and questions him.
units.rightText: The first to state his case seems right until another comes and cross-examines him.

units.leftText: The lot settles disputes, and keeps strong ones apart.
units.rightText: Casting the lot ends quarrels and separates strong opponents.

units.leftText: A brother offended is more difficult than a fortified city. Disputes are like the bars of a fortress.
units.rightText: An offended brother is harder to win than a fortified city, and disputes are like the bars of a castle.

units.leftText: A man’s stomach is filled with the fruit of his mouth. With the harvest of his lips he is satisfied.
units.rightText: From the fruit of his mouth a man’s belly is filled; with the harvest from his lips he is satisfied.

units.leftText: Death and life are in the power of the tongue; those who love it will eat its fruit.
units.rightText: Life and death are in the power of the tongue, and those who love it will eat its fruit.

units.leftText: Whoever finds a wife finds a good thing, and obtains favor of the LORD.
units.rightText: He who finds a wife finds a good thing and obtains favor from the LORD.

units.leftText: The poor plead for mercy, but the rich answer harshly.
units.rightText: The poor man pleads for mercy, but the rich man answers harshly.

units.leftText: A man of many companions may be ruined, but there is a friend who sticks closer than a brother.
units.rightText: A man of many companions may come to ruin, but there is a friend who stays closer than a brother.

units.leftText: Better is the poor who walks in his integrity than he who is perverse in his lips and is a fool.
units.rightText: Better a poor man who walks with integrity than a fool whose lips are perverse.

units.leftText: It isn’t good to have zeal without knowledge, nor to be hasty with one’s feet and miss the way.
units.rightText: Even zeal is no good without knowledge, and he who hurries his footsteps misses the mark.

units.leftText: The foolishness of man subverts his way; his heart rages against the LORD.
units.rightText: A man’s own folly subverts his way, yet his heart rages against the LORD.

units.leftText: Wealth adds many friends, but the poor is separated from his friend.
units.rightText: Wealth attracts many friends, but a poor man is deserted by his friend.

units.leftText: A false witness shall not be unpunished. He who pours out lies shall not go free.
units.rightText: A false witness will not go unpunished, and one who utters lies will not escape.

units.leftText: Many will entreat the favor of a ruler, and everyone is a friend to a man who gives gifts.
units.rightText: Many seek the favor of the prince, and everyone is a friend of the gift giver.

units.leftText: All the relatives of the poor shun him; how much more do his friends avoid him! He pursues them with pleas, but they are gone.
units.rightText: All the brothers of a poor man hate him — how much more do his friends avoid him! He may pursue them with pleading, but they are nowhere to be found.

units.leftText: He who gets wisdom loves his own soul. He who keeps understanding shall find good.
units.rightText: He who acquires wisdom loves himself; one who safeguards understanding will find success.

units.leftText: A false witness shall not be unpunished. He who utters lies shall perish.
units.rightText: A false witness will not go unpunished, and one who pours out lies will perish.

units.leftText: Delicate living is not appropriate for a fool, much less for a servant to have rule over princes.
units.rightText: Luxury is unseemly for a fool— how much worse for a slave to rule over princes!

units.leftText: The discretion of a man makes him slow to anger. It is his glory to overlook an offense.
units.rightText: A man’s insight gives him patience, and his virtue is to overlook an offense.

units.leftText: The king’s wrath is like the roaring of a lion, but his favor is like dew on the grass.
units.rightText: A king’s rage is like the roar of a lion, but his favor is like dew on the grass.

units.leftText: A foolish son is the calamity of his father. A wife’s quarrels are a continual dripping.
units.rightText: A foolish son is his father’s ruin, and a quarrelsome wife is like a constant dripping.

units.leftText: House and riches are an inheritance from fathers, but a prudent wife is from the LORD.
units.rightText: Houses and wealth are inherited from fathers, but a prudent wife is from the LORD.

units.leftText: Slothfulness casts into a deep sleep. The idle soul shall suffer hunger.
units.rightText: Laziness brings on deep sleep, and an idle soul will suffer hunger.

units.leftText: He who keeps the commandment keeps his soul, but he who is contemptuous in his ways shall die.
units.rightText: He who keeps a commandment preserves his soul, but he who is careless in his ways will die.

units.leftText: He who has pity on the poor lends to the LORD; he will reward him.
units.rightText: Kindness to the poor is a loan to the LORD, and He will repay the lender.

units.leftText: Discipline your son, for there is hope; don’t be a willing party to his death.
units.rightText: Discipline your son, for in that there is hope; do not be party to his death.

units.leftText: A hot-tempered man must pay the penalty, for if you rescue him, you must do it again.
units.rightText: A man of great anger must pay the penalty; if you rescue him, you will have to do so again.

units.leftText: Listen to counsel and receive instruction, that you may be wise in your latter end.
units.rightText: Listen to counsel and accept discipline, that you may be wise the rest of your days.

units.leftText: There are many plans in a man’s heart, but the LORD’s counsel will prevail.
units.rightText: Many plans are in a man’s heart, but the purpose of the LORD will prevail.

units.leftText: That which makes a man to be desired is his kindness. A poor man is better than a liar.
units.rightText: The desire of a man is loving devotion; better to be poor than a liar.

units.leftText: The fear of the LORD leads to life, then contentment; he rests and will not be touched by trouble.
units.rightText: The fear of the LORD leads to life, that one may rest content, without visitation from harm.

units.leftText: The sluggard buries his hand in the dish; he will not so much as bring it to his mouth again.
units.rightText: The slacker buries his hand in the dish; he will not even bring it back to his mouth.

units.leftText: Flog a scoffer, and the simple will learn prudence; rebuke one who has understanding, and he will gain knowledge.
units.rightText: Strike a mocker, and the simple will beware; rebuke the discerning man, and he will gain knowledge.

units.leftText: He who robs his father and drives away his mother is a son who causes shame and brings reproach.
units.rightText: He who assaults his father or evicts his mother is a son who brings shame and disgrace.

units.leftText: If you stop listening to instruction, my son, you will stray from the words of knowledge.
units.rightText: If you cease to hear instruction, my son, you will stray from the words of knowledge.

units.leftText: A corrupt witness mocks justice, and the mouth of the wicked gulps down iniquity.
units.rightText: A corrupt witness mocks justice, and a wicked mouth swallows iniquity.

units.leftText: Penalties are prepared for scoffers, and beatings for the backs of fools.
units.rightText: Judgments are prepared for mockers, and beatings for the backs of fools.

units.leftText: Wine is a mocker and beer is a brawler. Whoever is led astray by them is not wise.
units.rightText: Wine is a mocker, strong drink is a brawler, and whoever is led astray by them is not wise.

units.leftText: The terror of a king is like the roaring of a lion. He who provokes him to anger forfeits his own life.
units.rightText: The terror of a king is like the roar of a lion; whoever provokes him forfeits his own life.
rightNotes: 20:2 Literally sins against his own soul

units.leftText: It is an honor for a man to keep aloof from strife, but every fool will be quarreling.
units.rightText: It is honorable for a man to resolve a dispute, but any fool will quarrel.

units.leftText: The sluggard will not plow by reason of the winter; therefore he shall beg in harvest, and have nothing.
units.rightText: The slacker does not plow in season; at harvest time he looks, but nothing is there.

units.leftText: Counsel in the heart of man is like deep water, but a man of understanding will draw it out.
units.rightText: The intentions of a man’s heart are deep waters, but a man of understanding draws them out.

units.leftText: Many men claim to be men of unfailing love, but who can find a faithful man?
units.rightText: Many a man proclaims his loving devotion, but who can find a trustworthy man?

units.leftText: A righteous man walks in integrity. Blessed are his children after him.
units.rightText: The righteous man walks with integrity; blessed are his children after him.

units.leftText: A king who sits on the throne of judgment scatters away all evil with his eyes.
units.rightText: A king who sits on a throne to judge sifts out all evil with his eyes.

units.leftText: Who can say, “I have made my heart pure. I am clean and without sin”?
units.rightText: Who can say, “I have kept my heart pure; I am cleansed from my sin”?

units.leftText: Differing weights and differing measures, both of them alike are an abomination to the LORD.
units.rightText: Differing weights and unequal measures — both are detestable to the LORD.
rightNotes: 20:10 Hebrew A stone and a stone, an ephah and an ephah

units.leftText: Even a child makes himself known by his doings, whether his work is pure, and whether it is right.
units.rightText: Even a young man is known by his actions— whether his conduct is pure and upright.

units.leftText: The hearing ear, and the seeing eye, the LORD has made even both of them.
units.rightText: Ears that hear and eyes that see— the LORD has made them both.

units.leftText: Don’t love sleep, lest you come to poverty. Open your eyes, and you shall be satisfied with bread.
units.rightText: Do not love sleep, or you will grow poor; open your eyes, and you will have plenty of food.

units.leftText: “It’s no good, it’s no good,” says the buyer; but when he is gone his way, then he boasts.
units.rightText: “Worthless, worthless!” says the buyer, but on the way out, he gloats.

units.leftText: There is gold and abundance of rubies, but the lips of knowledge are a rare jewel.
units.rightText: There is an abundance of gold and rubies, but lips of knowledge are a rare treasure.

units.leftText: Take the garment of one who puts up collateral for a stranger; and hold him in pledge for a wayward woman.
units.rightText: Take the garment of the one who posts security for a stranger; get collateral if it is for a foreigner.
rightNotes: 20:16 Or a wayward woman

units.leftText: Fraudulent food is sweet to a man, but afterwards his mouth is filled with gravel.
units.rightText: Food gained by fraud is sweet to a man, but later his mouth is full of gravel.

units.leftText: Plans are established by advice; by wise guidance you wage war!
units.rightText: Set plans by consultation, and wage war under sound guidance.

units.leftText: He who goes about as a tale-bearer reveals secrets; therefore don’t keep company with him who opens wide his lips.
units.rightText: He who reveals secrets is a constant gossip; avoid the one who babbles with his lips.
rightNotes: 20:19 Or the one who is simple

units.leftText: Whoever curses his father or his mother, his lamp shall be put out in blackness of darkness.
units.rightText: Whoever curses his father or mother, his lamp will be extinguished in deepest darkness.

units.leftText: An inheritance quickly gained at the beginning won’t be blessed in the end.
units.rightText: An inheritance gained quickly will not be blessed in the end.

units.leftText: Don’t say, “I will pay back evil.” Wait for the LORD, and he will save you.
units.rightText: Do not say, “I will avenge this evil!” Wait on the LORD, and He will save you.

units.leftText: The LORD detests differing weights, and dishonest scales are not pleasing.
units.rightText: Unequal weights are detestable to the LORD, and dishonest scales are no good.

units.leftText: A man’s steps are from the LORD; how then can man understand his way?
units.rightText: A man’s steps are from the LORD, so how can anyone understand his own way?

units.leftText: It is a snare to a man to make a rash dedication, then later to consider his vows.
units.rightText: It is a trap for a man to dedicate something rashly, only later to reconsider his vows.

units.leftText: A wise king winnows out the wicked, and drives the threshing wheel over them.
units.rightText: A wise king separates out the wicked and drives the threshing wheel over them.

units.leftText: The spirit of man is the LORD’s lamp, searching all his innermost parts.
units.rightText: The spirit of a man is the lamp of the LORD, searching out his inmost being.
rightNotes: 20:27 Or breath or speech

units.leftText: Love and faithfulness keep the king safe. His throne is sustained by love.
units.rightText: Loving devotion and faithfulness preserve a king; by these he maintains his throne.

units.leftText: The glory of young men is their strength. The splendor of old men is their gray hair.
units.rightText: The glory of young men is their strength, and gray hair is the splendor of the old.

units.leftText: Wounding blows cleanse away evil, and beatings purge the innermost parts.
units.rightText: Lashes and wounds scour evil, and beatings cleanse the inmost parts.

units.leftText: The king’s heart is in the LORD’s hand like the watercourses. He turns it wherever he desires.
units.rightText: The king’s heart is a waterway in the hand of the LORD; He directs it where He pleases.

units.leftText: Every way of a man is right in his own eyes, but the LORD weighs the hearts.
units.rightText: All a man’s ways seem right to him, but the LORD weighs the heart.

units.leftText: To do righteousness and justice is more acceptable to the LORD than sacrifice.
units.rightText: To do righteousness and justice is more desirable to the LORD than sacrifice.

units.leftText: A high look and a proud heart, the lamp of the wicked, is sin.
units.rightText: Haughty eyes and a proud heart— the guides of the wicked— are sin.

units.leftText: The plans of the diligent surely lead to profit; and everyone who is hasty surely rushes to poverty.
units.rightText: The plans of the diligent bring plenty, as surely as haste leads to poverty.

units.leftText: Getting treasures by a lying tongue is a fleeting vapor for those who seek death.
units.rightText: Making a fortune by a lying tongue is a vanishing mist, a deadly pursuit.

units.leftText: The violence of the wicked will drive them away, because they refuse to do what is right.
units.rightText: The violence of the wicked will sweep them away because they refuse to do what is just.

units.leftText: The way of the guilty is devious, but the conduct of the innocent is upright.
units.rightText: The way of a guilty man is crooked, but the conduct of the innocent is upright.

units.leftText: It is better to dwell in the corner of the housetop than to share a house with a contentious woman.
units.rightText: Better to live on a corner of the roof than to share a house with a quarrelsome wife.

units.leftText: The soul of the wicked desires evil; his neighbor finds no mercy in his eyes.
units.rightText: The soul of the wicked man craves evil; his neighbor finds no favor in his eyes.

units.leftText: When the mocker is punished, the simple gains wisdom. When the wise is instructed, he receives knowledge.
units.rightText: When a mocker is punished, the simple gain wisdom; and when a wise man is instructed, he acquires knowledge.

units.leftText: The Righteous One considers the house of the wicked, and brings the wicked to ruin.
units.rightText: The Righteous One considers the house of the wicked and brings the wicked to ruin.
rightNotes: 21:12 Or The righteous one

units.leftText: Whoever stops his ears at the cry of the poor, he will also cry out, but shall not be heard.
units.rightText: Whoever shuts his ears to the cry of the poor, he too shall cry out and receive no answer.

units.leftText: A gift in secret pacifies anger, and a bribe in the cloak, strong wrath.
units.rightText: A gift in secret soothes anger, and a covert bribe pacifies great wrath.
rightNotes: 21:14 Hebrew a bribe in the bosom

units.leftText: It is joy to the righteous to do justice; but it is a destruction to the workers of iniquity.
units.rightText: Justice executed is a joy to the righteous, but a terror to the workers of iniquity.

units.leftText: The man who wanders out of the way of understanding shall rest in the assembly of the departed spirits.
units.rightText: The man who strays from the path of understanding will rest in the assembly of the dead.

units.leftText: He who loves pleasure will be a poor man. He who loves wine and oil won’t be rich.
units.rightText: He who loves pleasure will become poor; the one who loves wine and oil will never be rich.

units.leftText: The wicked is a ransom for the righteous, the treacherous for the upright.
units.rightText: The wicked become a ransom for the righteous, and the faithless for the upright.

units.leftText: It is better to dwell in a desert land, than with a contentious and fretful woman.
units.rightText: Better to live in the desert than with a contentious and ill-tempered wife.

units.leftText: There is precious treasure and oil in the dwelling of the wise, but a foolish man swallows it up.
units.rightText: Precious treasures and oil are in the dwelling of the wise, but a foolish man consumes them.

units.leftText: He who follows after righteousness and kindness finds life, righteousness, and honor.
units.rightText: He who pursues righteousness and loving devotion finds life, righteousness, and honor.

units.leftText: A wise man scales the city of the mighty, and brings down the strength of its confidence.
units.rightText: A wise man scales the city of the mighty and pulls down the stronghold in which they trust.

units.leftText: Whoever guards his mouth and his tongue keeps his soul from troubles.
units.rightText: He who guards his mouth and tongue keeps his soul from distress.

units.leftText: The proud and arrogant man—“Scoffer” is his name— he works in the arrogance of pride.
units.rightText: Mocker is the name of the proud and arrogant man — of him who acts with excessive pride.

units.leftText: The desire of the sluggard kills him, for his hands refuse to labor.
units.rightText: The craving of the slacker kills him because his hands refuse to work.

units.leftText: There are those who covet greedily all day long; but the righteous give and don’t withhold.
units.rightText: All day long he covets more, but the righteous give without restraint.

units.leftText: The sacrifice of the wicked is an abomination— how much more, when he brings it with a wicked mind!
units.rightText: The sacrifice of the wicked is detestable— how much more so when brought with ill intent!

units.leftText: A false witness will perish. A man who listens speaks to eternity.
units.rightText: A lying witness will perish, but the man who listens to truth will speak forever.

units.leftText: A wicked man hardens his face; but as for the upright, he establishes his ways.
units.rightText: A wicked man hardens his face, but the upright man makes his way sure.
rightNotes: 21:29 Or puts up a bold front

units.leftText: There is no wisdom nor understanding nor counsel against the LORD.
units.rightText: There is no wisdom, no understanding, no counsel that can prevail against the LORD.

units.leftText: The horse is prepared for the day of battle; but victory is with the LORD.
units.rightText: A horse is prepared for the day of battle, but victory is of the LORD.

units.leftText: A good name is more desirable than great riches, and loving favor is better than silver and gold.
units.rightText: A good name is more desirable than great riches; favor is better than silver and gold.

units.leftText: The rich and the poor have this in common: The LORD is the maker of them all.
units.rightText: The rich and the poor have this in common: The LORD is Maker of them all.

units.leftText: A prudent man sees danger and hides himself; but the simple pass on, and suffer for it.
units.rightText: The prudent see danger and take cover, but the simple keep going and suffer the consequences.

units.leftText: The result of humility and the fear of the LORD is wealth, honor, and life.
units.rightText: The rewards of humility and the fear of the LORD are wealth and honor and life.

units.leftText: Thorns and snares are in the path of the wicked; whoever guards his soul stays far from them.
units.rightText: Thorns and snares lie on the path of the perverse; he who guards his soul stays far from them.

units.leftText: Train up a child in the way he should go, and when he is old he will not depart from it.
units.rightText: Train up a child in the way he should go, and when he is old he will not depart from it.

units.leftText: The rich rule over the poor. The borrower is servant to the lender.
units.rightText: The rich rule over the poor, and the borrower is slave to the lender.

units.leftText: He who sows wickedness reaps trouble, and the rod of his fury will be destroyed.
units.rightText: He who sows injustice will reap disaster, and the rod of his fury will be destroyed.
rightNotes: 22:8 LXX includes God blesses a cheerful and generous man, but foolish works will come to an end; see also 2 Corinthians 9:7|2CO 9:7*.

units.leftText: He who has a generous eye will be blessed, for he shares his food with the poor.
units.rightText: A generous man will be blessed, for he shares his bread with the poor.
rightNotes: 22:9 Literally He whose eye is good

units.leftText: Drive out the mocker, and strife will go out; yes, quarrels and insults will stop.
units.rightText: Drive out the mocker, and conflict will depart; even quarreling and insults will cease.

units.leftText: He who loves purity of heart and speaks gracefully is the king’s friend.
units.rightText: He who loves a pure heart and gracious lips will have the king for a friend.

units.leftText: The LORD’s eyes watch over knowledge, but he frustrates the words of the unfaithful.
units.rightText: The LORD’s eyes keep watch over knowledge, but He frustrates the words of the faithless.

units.leftText: The sluggard says, “There is a lion outside! I will be killed in the streets!”
units.rightText: The slacker says, “There is a lion outside! I will be slain in the streets!”

units.leftText: The mouth of an adulteress is a deep pit. He who is under the LORD’s wrath will fall into it.
units.rightText: The mouth of an adulteress is a deep pit; he who is under the wrath of the LORD will fall into it.

units.leftText: Folly is bound up in the heart of a child; the rod of discipline drives it far from him.
units.rightText: Foolishness is bound up in the heart of a child, but the rod of discipline drives it far from him.

units.leftText: Whoever oppresses the poor for his own increase and whoever gives to the rich, both come to poverty.
units.rightText: Oppressing the poor to enrich oneself or giving gifts to the rich will surely lead to poverty. Thirty Sayings of the Wise Saying 1

units.leftText: Turn your ear, and listen to the words of the wise. Apply your heart to my teaching.
units.rightText: Incline your ear and hear the words of the wise — apply your mind to my knowledge —

units.leftText: For it is a pleasant thing if you keep them within you, if all of them are ready on your lips.
units.rightText: for it is pleasing when you keep them within you and they are constantly on your lips.

units.leftText: I teach you today, even you, so that your trust may be in the LORD.
units.rightText: So that your trust may be in the LORD, I instruct you today — yes, you.

units.leftText: Haven’t I written to you thirty excellent things of counsel and knowledge,
units.rightText: Have I not written for you thirty sayings about counsel and knowledge,
rightNotes: 22:20 Or written for you excellent sayings or written for you three times

units.leftText: To teach you truth, reliable words, to give sound answers to the ones who sent you?
units.rightText: to show you true and reliable words, that you may soundly answer those who sent you? Saying 2

units.leftText: Don’t exploit the poor because he is poor; and don’t crush the needy in court;
units.rightText: Do not rob a poor man because he is poor, and do not crush the afflicted at the gate,

units.leftText: for the LORD will plead their case, and plunder the life of those who plunder them.
units.rightText: for the LORD will take up their case and will plunder those who rob them. Saying 3

units.leftText: Don’t befriend a hot-tempered man. Don’t associate with one who harbors anger,
units.rightText: Do not make friends with an angry man, and do not associate with a hot-tempered man,

units.leftText: lest you learn his ways and ensnare your soul.
units.rightText: or you may learn his ways and entangle yourself in a snare. Saying 4

units.leftText: Don’t you be one of those who strike hands, of those who are collateral for debts.
units.rightText: Do not be one who gives pledges, who puts up security for debts.

units.leftText: If you don’t have means to pay, why should he take away your bed from under you?
units.rightText: If you have nothing with which to pay, why should your bed be taken from under you? Saying 5

units.leftText: Don’t move the ancient boundary stone which your fathers have set up.
units.rightText: Do not move an ancient boundary stone which your fathers have placed. Saying 6

units.leftText: Do you see a man skilled in his work? He will serve kings. He won’t serve obscure men.
units.rightText: Do you see a man skilled in his work? He will be stationed in the presence of kings; he will not stand before obscure men.

units.leftText: When you sit to eat with a ruler, consider diligently what is before you;
units.rightText: When you sit down to dine with a ruler, consider carefully what is set before you,
rightNotes: 23:1 Or who is before you

units.leftText: put a knife to your throat if you are a man given to appetite.
units.rightText: and put a knife to your throat if you possess a great appetite.

units.leftText: Don’t be desirous of his dainties, since they are deceitful food.
units.rightText: Do not crave his delicacies, for that food is deceptive. Saying 8

units.leftText: Don’t weary yourself to be rich. In your wisdom, show restraint.
units.rightText: Do not wear yourself out to get rich; be wise enough to restrain yourself.

units.leftText: Why do you set your eyes on that which is not? For it certainly sprouts wings like an eagle and flies in the sky.
units.rightText: When you glance at wealth, it disappears, for it makes wings for itself and flies like an eagle to the sky. Saying 9

units.leftText: Don’t eat the food of him who has a stingy eye, and don’t crave his delicacies,
units.rightText: Do not eat the bread of a stingy man, and do not crave his delicacies;
rightNotes: 23:6 Literally of him whose eye is evil

units.leftText: for as he thinks about the cost, so he is. “Eat and drink!” he says to you, but his heart is not with you.
units.rightText: for he is keeping track, inwardly counting the cost. “Eat and drink,” he says to you, but his heart is not with you.
rightNotes: 23:7 Or for as he calculates in his soul, so is he

units.leftText: You will vomit up the morsel which you have eaten and waste your pleasant words.
units.rightText: You will vomit up what little you have eaten and waste your pleasant words. Saying 10

units.leftText: Don’t speak in the ears of a fool, for he will despise the wisdom of your words.
units.rightText: Do not speak to a fool, for he will despise the wisdom of your words. Saying 11

units.leftText: Don’t move the ancient boundary stone. Don’t encroach on the fields of the fatherless,
units.rightText: Do not move an ancient boundary stone or encroach on the fields of the fatherless,

units.leftText: for their Defender is strong. He will plead their case against you.
units.rightText: for their Redeemer is strong; He will take up their case against you. Saying 12

units.leftText: Apply your heart to instruction, and your ears to the words of knowledge.
units.rightText: Apply your heart to instruction and your ears to words of knowledge. Saying 13

units.leftText: Don’t withhold correction from a child. If you punish him with the rod, he will not die.
units.rightText: Do not withhold discipline from a child; although you strike him with a rod, he will not die.

units.leftText: Punish him with the rod, and save his soul from Sheol.
units.rightText: Strike him with a rod, and you will deliver his soul from Sheol. Saying 14
leftNotes: 23:14 Sheol is the place of the dead.

units.leftText: My son, if your heart is wise, then my heart will be glad, even mine.
units.rightText: My son, if your heart is wise, my own heart will indeed rejoice.

units.leftText: Yes, my heart will rejoice when your lips speak what is right.
units.rightText: My inmost being will rejoice when your lips speak what is right. Saying 15
rightNotes: 23:16 Hebrew My kidneys

units.leftText: Don’t let your heart envy sinners, but rather fear the LORD all day long.
units.rightText: Do not let your heart envy sinners, but always continue in the fear of the LORD.

units.leftText: Indeed surely there is a future hope, and your hope will not be cut off.
units.rightText: For surely there is a future, and your hope will not be cut off. Saying 16

units.leftText: Listen, my son, and be wise, and keep your heart on the right path!
units.rightText: Listen, my son, and be wise, and guide your heart on the right course.

units.leftText: Don’t be among ones drinking too much wine, or those who gorge themselves on meat;
units.rightText: Do not join those who drink too much wine or gorge themselves on meat.

units.leftText: for the drunkard and the glutton shall become poor; and drowsiness clothes them in rags.
units.rightText: For the drunkard and the glutton will come to poverty, and drowsiness will clothe them in rags. Saying 17

units.leftText: Listen to your father who gave you life, and don’t despise your mother when she is old.
units.rightText: Listen to your father who gave you life, and do not despise your mother when she is old.

units.leftText: Buy the truth, and don’t sell it. Get wisdom, discipline, and understanding.
units.rightText: Invest in truth and never sell it— in wisdom and instruction and understanding.

units.leftText: The father of the righteous has great joy. Whoever fathers a wise child delights in him.
units.rightText: The father of a righteous man will greatly rejoice, and he who fathers a wise son will delight in him.

units.leftText: Let your father and your mother be glad! Let her who bore you rejoice!
units.rightText: May your father and mother be glad, and may she who gave you birth rejoice! Saying 18

units.leftText: My son, give me your heart; and let your eyes keep in my ways.
units.rightText: My son, give me your heart, and let your eyes delight in my ways.

units.leftText: For a prostitute is a deep pit; and a wayward wife is a narrow well.
units.rightText: For a prostitute is a deep pit, and an adulteress is a narrow well.
rightNotes: 23:27 Or a foreign woman or a wayward wife

units.leftText: Yes, she lies in wait like a robber, and increases the unfaithful among men.
units.rightText: Like a robber she lies in wait and multiplies the faithless among men. Saying 19

units.leftText: Who has woe? Who has sorrow? Who has strife? Who has complaints? Who has needless bruises? Who has bloodshot eyes?
units.rightText: Who has woe? Who has sorrow? Who has contentions? Who has complaints? Who has needless wounds? Who has bloodshot eyes?

units.leftText: Those who stay long at the wine; those who go to seek out mixed wine.
units.rightText: Those who linger over wine, who go to taste mixed drinks.

units.leftText: Don’t look at the wine when it is red, when it sparkles in the cup, when it goes down smoothly.
units.rightText: Do not gaze at wine while it is red, when it sparkles in the cup and goes down smoothly.

units.leftText: In the end, it bites like a snake, and poisons like a viper.
units.rightText: In the end it bites like a snake and stings like a viper.

units.leftText: Your eyes will see strange things, and your mind will imagine confusing things.
units.rightText: Your eyes will see strange things, and your mind will utter perversities.

units.leftText: Yes, you will be as he who lies down in the middle of the sea, or as he who lies on top of the rigging:
units.rightText: You will be like one sleeping on the high seas or lying on the top of a mast:

units.leftText: “They hit me, and I was not hurt! They beat me, and I don’t feel it! When will I wake up? I can do it again. I will look for more.”
units.rightText: “They struck me, but I feel no pain! They beat me, but I did not know it! When can I wake up to search for another drink?”

units.leftText: Don’t be envious of evil men, neither desire to be with them;
units.rightText: Do not envy wicked men or desire their company;

units.leftText: for their hearts plot violence and their lips talk about mischief.
units.rightText: for their hearts devise violence, and their lips declare trouble. Saying 21

units.leftText: Through wisdom a house is built; by understanding it is established;
units.rightText: By wisdom a house is built and by understanding it is established;

units.leftText: by knowledge the rooms are filled with all rare and beautiful treasure.
units.rightText: through knowledge its rooms are filled with every precious and beautiful treasure. Saying 22

units.leftText: A wise man has great power. A knowledgeable man increases strength,
units.rightText: A wise man is strong, and a man of knowledge enhances his strength.
rightNotes: 24:5 LXX The wise are mightier than the strong

units.leftText: for by wise guidance you wage your war, and victory is in many advisors.
units.rightText: Only with sound guidance should you wage war, and victory lies in a multitude of counselors. Saying 23

units.leftText: Wisdom is too high for a fool. He doesn’t open his mouth in the gate.
units.rightText: Wisdom is too high for a fool; he does not open his mouth in the meeting place. Saying 24

units.leftText: One who plots to do evil will be called a schemer.
units.rightText: He who plots evil will be called a schemer.

units.leftText: The schemes of folly are sin. The mocker is detested by men.
units.rightText: A foolish scheme is sin, and a mocker is detestable to men. Saying 25

units.leftText: If you falter in the time of trouble, your strength is small.
units.rightText: If you faint in the day of distress, how small is your strength!

units.leftText: Rescue those who are being led away to death! Indeed, hold back those who are staggering to the slaughter!
units.rightText: Rescue those being led away to death, and restrain those stumbling toward the slaughter.

units.leftText: If you say, “Behold, we didn’t know this,” doesn’t he who weighs the hearts consider it? He who keeps your soul, doesn’t he know it? Shall he not give to every man according to his work?
units.rightText: If you say, “Behold, we did not know about this,” does not He who weighs hearts consider it? Does not the One who guards your life know? Will He not repay a man according to his deeds? Saying 26

units.leftText: My son, eat honey, for it is good, the droppings of the honeycomb, which are sweet to your taste;
units.rightText: Eat honey, my son, for it is good, and the honeycomb is sweet to your taste.

units.leftText: so you shall know wisdom to be to your soul. If you have found it, then there will be a reward: Your hope will not be cut off.
units.rightText: Know therefore that wisdom is sweet to your soul. If you find it, there is a future for you, and your hope will never be cut off. Saying 27

units.leftText: Don’t lay in wait, wicked man, against the habitation of the righteous. Don’t destroy his resting place;
units.rightText: Do not lie in wait, O wicked man, near the dwelling of the righteous; do not destroy his resting place.

units.leftText: for a righteous man falls seven times and rises up again, but the wicked are overthrown by calamity.
units.rightText: For though a righteous man may fall seven times, he still gets up; but the wicked stumble in bad times. Saying 28

units.leftText: Don’t rejoice when your enemy falls. Don’t let your heart be glad when he is overthrown,
units.rightText: Do not gloat when your enemy falls, and do not let your heart rejoice when he stumbles,

units.leftText: lest the LORD see it, and it displease him, and he turn away his wrath from him.
units.rightText: or the LORD will see and disapprove, and turn His wrath away from him. Saying 29

units.leftText: Don’t fret yourself because of evildoers, neither be envious of the wicked;
units.rightText: Do not fret over evildoers, and do not be envious of the wicked.

units.leftText: for there will be no reward to the evil man. The lamp of the wicked will be snuffed out.
units.rightText: For the evil man has no future; the lamp of the wicked will be extinguished. Saying 30

units.leftText: My son, fear the LORD and the king. Don’t join those who are rebellious,
units.rightText: My son, fear the LORD and the king, and do not associate with the rebellious.

units.leftText: for their calamity will rise suddenly. Who knows what destruction may come from them both?
units.rightText: For they will bring sudden destruction. Who knows what ruin they can bring? Further Sayings of the Wise

units.leftText: These also are sayings of the wise: To show partiality in judgment is not good.
units.rightText: These also are sayings of the wise: To show partiality in judgment is not good.

units.leftText: He who says to the wicked, “You are righteous,” peoples will curse him, and nations will abhor him—
units.rightText: Whoever tells the guilty, “You are innocent”— peoples will curse him, and nations will denounce him;

units.leftText: but it will go well with those who convict the guilty, and a rich blessing will come on them.
units.rightText: but it will go well with those who convict the guilty, and rich blessing will come upon them.

units.leftText: An honest answer is like a kiss on the lips.
units.rightText: An honest answer given is like a kiss on the lips.

units.leftText: Prepare your work outside, and get your fields ready. Afterwards, build your house.
units.rightText: Complete your outdoor work and prepare your field; after that, you may build your house.

units.leftText: Don’t be a witness against your neighbor without cause. Don’t deceive with your lips.
units.rightText: Do not testify against your neighbor without cause, and do not deceive with your lips.

units.leftText: Don’t say, “I will do to him as he has done to me; I will repay the man according to his work.”
units.rightText: Do not say, “I will do to him as he has done to me; I will repay the man according to his work.”

units.leftText: I went by the field of the sluggard, by the vineyard of the man void of understanding.
units.rightText: I went past the field of a slacker and by the vineyard of a man lacking judgment.

units.leftText: Behold, it was all grown over with thorns. Its surface was covered with nettles, and its stone wall was broken down.
units.rightText: Thorns had grown up everywhere, thistles had covered the ground, and the stone wall was broken down.

units.leftText: Then I saw, and considered well. I saw, and received instruction:
units.rightText: I observed and took it to heart; I looked and received instruction:

units.leftText: a little sleep, a little slumber, a little folding of the hands to sleep,
units.rightText: A little sleep, a little slumber, a little folding of the hands to rest,

units.leftText: so your poverty will come as a robber and your want as an armed man.
units.rightText: and poverty will come upon you like a robber, and need like a bandit.

units.leftText: These also are proverbs of Solomon, which the men of Hezekiah king of Judah copied out.
units.rightText: These are additional proverbs of Solomon, which were copied by the men of Hezekiah king of Judah:

units.leftText: It is the glory of God to conceal a thing, but the glory of kings is to search out a matter.
units.rightText: It is the glory of God to conceal a matter and the glory of kings to search it out.

units.leftText: As the heavens for height, and the earth for depth, so the hearts of kings are unsearchable.
units.rightText: As the heavens are high and the earth is deep, so the hearts of kings cannot be searched.

units.leftText: Take away the dross from the silver, and material comes out for the refiner.
units.rightText: Remove the dross from the silver, and a vessel for a silversmith will come forth.

units.leftText: Take away the wicked from the king’s presence, and his throne will be established in righteousness.
units.rightText: Remove the wicked from the king’s presence, and his throne will be established in righteousness.

units.leftText: Don’t exalt yourself in the presence of the king, or claim a place among great men;
units.rightText: Do not exalt yourself in the presence of the king, and do not stand in the place of great men;

units.leftText: for it is better that it be said to you, “Come up here,” than that you should be put lower in the presence of the prince, whom your eyes have seen.
units.rightText: for it is better to be told, “Come up here!” than to be demoted in the presence of the prince. Even what you have seen with your own eyes,
rightNotes: 25:7 Or Even the one

units.leftText: Don’t be hasty in bringing charges to court. What will you do in the end when your neighbor shames you?
units.rightText: do not bring hastily to court. Otherwise, what will you do in the end when your neighbor puts you to shame?

units.leftText: Debate your case with your neighbor, and don’t betray the confidence of another,
units.rightText: Argue your case with your neighbor without betraying another’s confidence,

units.leftText: lest one who hears it put you to shame, and your bad reputation never depart.
units.rightText: lest he who hears you bring shame upon you, and your infamy never go away.

units.leftText: A word fitly spoken is like apples of gold in settings of silver.
units.rightText: A word fitly spoken is like apples of gold in settings of silver.

units.leftText: As an earring of gold, and an ornament of fine gold, so is a wise reprover to an obedient ear.
units.rightText: Like an earring of gold or an ornament of fine gold is a wise man’s rebuke to a listening ear.

units.leftText: As the cold of snow in the time of harvest, so is a faithful messenger to those who send him; for he refreshes the soul of his masters.
units.rightText: Like the cold of snow in the time of harvest is a trustworthy messenger to those who send him; he refreshes the soul of his masters.

units.leftText: As clouds and wind without rain, so is he who boasts of gifts deceptively.
units.rightText: Like clouds and wind without rain is the man who boasts of gifts never given.

units.leftText: By patience a ruler is persuaded. A soft tongue breaks the bone.
units.rightText: Through patience a ruler can be persuaded, and a gentle tongue can break a bone.

units.leftText: Have you found honey? Eat as much as is sufficient for you, lest you eat too much, and vomit it.
units.rightText: If you find honey, eat just what you need, lest you have too much and vomit it up.

units.leftText: Let your foot be seldom in your neighbor’s house, lest he be weary of you, and hate you.
units.rightText: Seldom set foot in your neighbor’s house, lest he grow weary and hate you.

units.leftText: A man who gives false testimony against his neighbor is like a club, a sword, or a sharp arrow.
units.rightText: Like a club or sword or sharp arrow is a man who bears false witness against his neighbor.

units.leftText: Confidence in someone unfaithful in time of trouble is like a bad tooth or a lame foot.
units.rightText: Like a broken tooth or a foot out of joint is confidence in a faithless man in time of trouble.

units.leftText: As one who takes away a garment in cold weather, or vinegar on soda, so is one who sings songs to a heavy heart.
units.rightText: Like one who removes a garment on a cold day or vinegar poured on a wound is one who sings songs to a heavy heart.
rightNotes: 25:20 Or on soda

units.leftText: If your enemy is hungry, give him food to eat. If he is thirsty, give him water to drink;
units.rightText: If your enemy is hungry, give him food to eat, and if he is thirsty, give him water to drink.

units.leftText: for you will heap coals of fire on his head, and the LORD will reward you.
units.rightText: For in so doing, you will heap burning coals on his head, and the LORD will reward you.
rightNotes: 25:22 LXX; Hebrew For you will heap burning coals on his head; cited in Romans 12:20|ROM 12:20*

units.leftText: The north wind produces rain; so a backbiting tongue brings an angry face.
units.rightText: As the north wind brings forth rain, so a backbiting tongue brings angry looks.

units.leftText: It is better to dwell in the corner of the housetop than to share a house with a contentious woman.
units.rightText: Better to live on a corner of the roof than to share a house with a quarrelsome wife.

units.leftText: Like cold water to a thirsty soul, so is good news from a far country.
units.rightText: Like cold water to a weary soul is good news from a distant land.

units.leftText: Like a muddied spring and a polluted well, so is a righteous man who gives way before the wicked.
units.rightText: Like a muddied spring or a polluted well is a righteous man who gives way to the wicked.

units.leftText: It is not good to eat much honey, nor is it honorable to seek one’s own honor.
units.rightText: It is not good to eat too much honey or to search out one’s own glory.

units.leftText: Like a city that is broken down and without walls is a man whose spirit is without restraint.
units.rightText: Like a city whose walls are broken down is a man who does not control his temper.

units.leftText: Like snow in summer, and as rain in harvest, so honor is not fitting for a fool.
units.rightText: Like snow in summer and rain at harvest, honor does not befit a fool.

units.leftText: Like a fluttering sparrow, like a darting swallow, so the undeserved curse doesn’t come to rest.
units.rightText: Like a fluttering sparrow or darting swallow, an undeserved curse does not come to rest.

units.leftText: A whip is for the horse, a bridle for the donkey, and a rod for the back of fools!
units.rightText: A whip for the horse, a bridle for the donkey, and a rod for the backs of fools!

units.leftText: Don’t answer a fool according to his folly, lest you also be like him.
units.rightText: Do not answer a fool according to his folly, or you yourself will be like him.

units.leftText: Answer a fool according to his folly, lest he be wise in his own eyes.
units.rightText: Answer a fool according to his folly, lest he become wise in his own eyes.

units.leftText: One who sends a message by the hand of a fool is cutting off feet and drinking violence.
units.rightText: Like cutting off one’s own feet or drinking violence is the sending of a message by the hand of a fool.

units.leftText: Like the legs of the lame that hang loose, so is a parable in the mouth of fools.
units.rightText: Like lame legs hanging limp is a proverb in the mouth of a fool.

units.leftText: As one who binds a stone in a sling, so is he who gives honor to a fool.
units.rightText: Like binding a stone into a sling is the giving of honor to a fool.

units.leftText: Like a thorn bush that goes into the hand of a drunkard, so is a parable in the mouth of fools.
units.rightText: Like a thorn that goes into the hand of a drunkard is a proverb in the mouth of a fool.

units.leftText: As an archer who wounds all, so is he who hires a fool or he who hires those who pass by.
units.rightText: Like an archer who wounds at random is he who hires a fool or passerby.

units.leftText: As a dog that returns to his vomit, so is a fool who repeats his folly.
units.rightText: As a dog returns to its vomit, so a fool repeats his folly.
rightNotes: 26:11 Cited in 2 Peter 2:22|2PE 2:22*

units.leftText: Do you see a man wise in his own eyes? There is more hope for a fool than for him.
units.rightText: Do you see a man who is wise in his own eyes? There is more hope for a fool than for him.

units.leftText: The sluggard says, “There is a lion in the road! A fierce lion roams the streets!”
units.rightText: The slacker says, “A lion is in the road! A fierce lion roams the public square!”

units.leftText: As the door turns on its hinges, so does the sluggard on his bed.
units.rightText: As a door turns on its hinges, so the slacker turns on his bed.

units.leftText: The sluggard buries his hand in the dish. He is too lazy to bring it back to his mouth.
units.rightText: The slacker buries his hand in the dish; it wearies him to bring it back to his mouth.

units.leftText: The sluggard is wiser in his own eyes than seven men who answer with discretion.
units.rightText: The slacker is wiser in his own eyes than seven men who answer discreetly.

units.leftText: Like one who grabs a dog’s ears is one who passes by and meddles in a quarrel not his own.
units.rightText: Like one who grabs a dog by the ears is a passerby who meddles in a quarrel not his own.

units.leftText: Like a madman who shoots torches, arrows, and death,
units.rightText: Like a madman shooting firebrands and deadly arrows,

units.leftText: is the man who deceives his neighbor and says, “Am I not joking?”
units.rightText: so is the man who deceives his neighbor and says, “I was only joking!”

units.leftText: For lack of wood a fire goes out. Without gossip, a quarrel dies down.
units.rightText: Without wood, a fire goes out; without gossip, a conflict ceases.

units.leftText: As coals are to hot embers, and wood to fire, so is a contentious man to kindling strife.
units.rightText: Like charcoal for embers and wood for fire, so is a quarrelsome man for kindling strife.

units.leftText: The words of a whisperer are as dainty morsels, they go down into the innermost parts.
units.rightText: The words of a gossip are like choice morsels that go down into the inmost being.

units.leftText: Like silver dross on an earthen vessel are the lips of a fervent one with an evil heart.
units.rightText: Like glaze covering an earthen vessel are burning lips and a wicked heart.
rightNotes: 26:23 Hebrew; LXX smooth

units.leftText: A malicious man disguises himself with his lips, but he harbors evil in his heart.
units.rightText: A hateful man disguises himself with his speech, but he lays up deceit in his heart.

units.leftText: When his speech is charming, don’t believe him, for there are seven abominations in his heart.
units.rightText: When he speaks graciously, do not believe him, for seven abominations fill his heart.

units.leftText: His malice may be concealed by deception, but his wickedness will be exposed in the assembly.
units.rightText: Though his hatred is concealed by deception, his wickedness will be exposed in the assembly.

units.leftText: Whoever digs a pit shall fall into it. Whoever rolls a stone, it will come back on him.
units.rightText: He who digs a pit will fall into it, and he who rolls a stone will have it roll back on him.

units.leftText: A lying tongue hates those it hurts; and a flattering mouth works ruin.
units.rightText: A lying tongue hates those it crushes, and a flattering mouth causes ruin.

units.leftText: Don’t boast about tomorrow; for you don’t know what a day may bring.
units.rightText: Do not boast about tomorrow, for you do not know what a day may bring.

units.leftText: Let another man praise you, and not your own mouth; a stranger, and not your own lips.
units.rightText: Let another praise you, and not your own mouth— a stranger, and not your own lips.

units.leftText: A stone is heavy, and sand is a burden; but a fool’s provocation is heavier than both.
units.rightText: A stone is heavy and sand is a burden, but aggravation from a fool outweighs them both.

units.leftText: Wrath is cruel, and anger is overwhelming; but who is able to stand before jealousy?
units.rightText: Wrath is cruel and anger is like a flood, but who can withstand jealousy?

units.leftText: Better is open rebuke than hidden love.
units.rightText: Better an open rebuke than love that is concealed.

units.leftText: The wounds of a friend are faithful, although the kisses of an enemy are profuse.
units.rightText: The wounds of a friend are faithful, but the kisses of an enemy are deceitful.

units.leftText: A full soul loathes a honeycomb; but to a hungry soul, every bitter thing is sweet.
units.rightText: The soul that is full loathes honey, but to a hungry soul, any bitter thing is sweet.

units.leftText: As a bird that wanders from her nest, so is a man who wanders from his home.
units.rightText: Like a bird that strays from its nest is a man who wanders from his home.

units.leftText: Perfume and incense bring joy to the heart; so does earnest counsel from a man’s friend.
units.rightText: Oil and incense bring joy to the heart, and the counsel of a friend is sweetness to the soul.

units.leftText: Don’t forsake your friend and your father’s friend. Don’t go to your brother’s house in the day of your disaster. A neighbor who is near is better than a distant brother.
units.rightText: Do not forsake your friend or your father’s friend, and do not go to your brother’s house in the day of your calamity; better a neighbor nearby than a brother far away.

units.leftText: Be wise, my son, and bring joy to my heart, then I can answer my tormentor.
