units.rightText: Be wise, my son, and bring joy to my heart, so that I can answer him who taunts me.

units.leftText: A prudent man sees danger and takes refuge; but the simple pass on, and suffer for it.
units.rightText: The prudent see danger and take cover, but the simple keep going and pay the penalty.

units.leftText: Take his garment when he puts up collateral for a stranger. Hold it for a wayward woman!
units.rightText: Take the garment of him who posts security for a stranger; get collateral if it is for a foreigner.
rightNotes: 27:13 Or a wayward woman

units.leftText: He who blesses his neighbor with a loud voice early in the morning, it will be taken as a curse by him.
units.rightText: If one blesses his neighbor with a loud voice early in the morning, it will be counted to him as a curse.

units.leftText: A continual dropping on a rainy day and a contentious wife are alike:
units.rightText: A constant dripping on a rainy day and a contentious woman are alike —

units.leftText: restraining her is like restraining the wind, or like grasping oil in his right hand.
units.rightText: restraining her is like holding back the wind or grasping oil with one’s right hand.

units.leftText: Iron sharpens iron; so a man sharpens his friend’s countenance.
units.rightText: As iron sharpens iron, so one man sharpens another.
rightNotes: 27:17 Hebrew sharpens the face of another or sharpens the countenance of a friend

units.leftText: Whoever tends the fig tree shall eat its fruit. He who looks after his master shall be honored.
units.rightText: Whoever tends a fig tree will eat its fruit, and he who looks after his master will be honored.

units.leftText: Like water reflects a face, so a man’s heart reflects the man.
units.rightText: As water reflects the face, so the heart reflects the true man.

units.leftText: Sheol and Abaddon are never satisfied; and a man’s eyes are never satisfied.
units.rightText: Sheol and Abaddon are never satisfied; so the eyes of man are never satisfied.
leftNotes: 27:20 Sheol is the place of the dead.
rightNotes: 27:20 Or Death and Destruction

units.leftText: The crucible is for silver, and the furnace for gold; but man is refined by his praise.
units.rightText: A crucible for silver and a furnace for gold, but a man is tested by the praise accorded him.

units.leftText: Though you grind a fool in a mortar with a pestle along with grain, yet his foolishness will not be removed from him.
units.rightText: Though you grind a fool like grain with mortar and a pestle, yet his folly will not depart from him.

units.leftText: Know well the state of your flocks, and pay attention to your herds,
units.rightText: Be sure to know the state of your flocks, and pay close attention to your herds;

units.leftText: for riches are not forever, nor does the crown endure to all generations.
units.rightText: for riches are not forever, nor does a crown endure to every generation.

units.leftText: The hay is removed, and the new growth appears, the grasses of the hills are gathered in.
units.rightText: When hay is removed and new growth appears and the grass from the hills is gathered,

units.leftText: The lambs are for your clothing, and the goats are the price of a field.
units.rightText: the lambs will provide you with clothing, and the goats with the price of a field.

units.leftText: There will be plenty of goats’ milk for your food, for your family’s food, and for the nourishment of your servant girls.
units.rightText: You will have plenty of goats’ milk to feed you— food for your household and nourishment for your maidservants.

units.leftText: The wicked flee when no one pursues; but the righteous are as bold as a lion.
units.rightText: The wicked flee when no one pursues, but the righteous are as bold as a lion.

units.leftText: In rebellion, a land has many rulers, but order is maintained by a man of understanding and knowledge.
units.rightText: A land in rebellion has many rulers, but a man of understanding and knowledge maintains order.

units.leftText: A needy man who oppresses the poor is like a driving rain which leaves no crops.
units.rightText: A destitute leader who oppresses the poor is like a driving rain that leaves no food.

units.leftText: Those who forsake the law praise the wicked; but those who keep the law contend with them.
units.rightText: Those who forsake the law praise the wicked, but those who keep the law resist them.

units.leftText: Evil men don’t understand justice; but those who seek the LORD understand it fully.
units.rightText: Evil men do not understand justice, but those who seek the LORD comprehend fully.

units.leftText: Better is the poor who walks in his integrity than he who is perverse in his ways, and he is rich.
units.rightText: Better a poor man who walks with integrity than a rich man whose ways are perverse.

units.leftText: Whoever keeps the law is a wise son; but he who is a companion of gluttons shames his father.
units.rightText: A discerning son keeps the law, but a companion of gluttons disgraces his father.

units.leftText: He who increases his wealth by excessive interest gathers it for one who has pity on the poor.
units.rightText: He who increases his wealth by interest and usury lays it up for one who is kind to the poor.

units.leftText: He who turns away his ear from hearing the law, even his prayer is an abomination.
units.rightText: Whoever turns his ear away from hearing the law, even his prayer is detestable.

units.leftText: Whoever causes the upright to go astray in an evil way, he will fall into his own trap; but the blameless will inherit good.
units.rightText: He who leads the upright along the path of evil will fall into his own pit, but the blameless will inherit what is good.

units.leftText: The rich man is wise in his own eyes; but the poor who has understanding sees through him.
units.rightText: A rich man is wise in his own eyes, but a poor man with discernment sees through him.

units.leftText: When the righteous triumph, there is great glory; but when the wicked rise, men hide themselves.
units.rightText: When the righteous triumph, there is great glory, but when the wicked rise, men hide themselves.

units.leftText: He who conceals his sins doesn’t prosper, but whoever confesses and renounces them finds mercy.
units.rightText: He who conceals his sins will not prosper, but whoever confesses and renounces them will find mercy.

units.leftText: Blessed is the man who always fears; but one who hardens his heart falls into trouble.
units.rightText: Blessed is the man who is always reverent, but he who hardens his heart falls into trouble.
rightNotes: 28:14 Or always fears the LORD; Hebrew does not include the LORD.

units.leftText: As a roaring lion or a charging bear, so is a wicked ruler over helpless people.
units.rightText: Like a roaring lion or a charging bear is a wicked ruler over a helpless people.

units.leftText: A tyrannical ruler lacks judgment. One who hates ill-gotten gain will have long days.
units.rightText: A leader who lacks judgment is also a great oppressor, but he who hates dishonest profit will prolong his days.

units.leftText: A man who is tormented by blood guilt will be a fugitive until death. No one will support him.
units.rightText: A man burdened by bloodguilt will flee into the Pit; let no one support him.
rightNotes: 28:17 Or will be a fugitive until death

units.leftText: Whoever walks blamelessly is kept safe; but one with perverse ways will fall suddenly.
units.rightText: He who walks with integrity will be kept safe, but whoever is perverse in his ways will suddenly fall.

units.leftText: One who works his land will have an abundance of food; but one who chases fantasies will have his fill of poverty.
units.rightText: The one who works his land will have plenty of food, but whoever chases fantasies will have his fill of poverty.

units.leftText: A faithful man is rich with blessings; but one who is eager to be rich will not go unpunished.
units.rightText: A faithful man will abound with blessings, but one eager to be rich will not go unpunished.

units.leftText: To show partiality is not good, yet a man will do wrong for a piece of bread.
units.rightText: To show partiality is not good, yet a man will do wrong for a piece of bread.

units.leftText: A stingy man hurries after riches, and doesn’t know that poverty waits for him.
units.rightText: A stingy man hastens after wealth and does not know that poverty awaits him.
rightNotes: 28:22 Hebrew A man whose eye is evil

units.leftText: One who rebukes a man will afterward find more favor than one who flatters with the tongue.
units.rightText: He who rebukes a man will later find more favor than one who flatters with his tongue.

units.leftText: Whoever robs his father or his mother and says, “It’s not wrong,” is a partner with a destroyer.
units.rightText: He who robs his father or mother, saying, “It is not wrong,” is a companion to the man who destroys.

units.leftText: One who is greedy stirs up strife; but one who trusts in the LORD will prosper.
units.rightText: A greedy man stirs up strife, but he who trusts in the LORD will prosper.

units.leftText: One who trusts in himself is a fool; but one who walks in wisdom is kept safe.
units.rightText: He who trusts in himself is a fool, but one who walks in wisdom will be safe.

units.leftText: One who gives to the poor has no lack; but one who closes his eyes will have many curses.
units.rightText: Whoever gives to the poor will not be in need, but he who hides his eyes will receive many curses.

units.leftText: When the wicked rise, men hide themselves; but when they perish, the righteous thrive.
units.rightText: When the wicked come to power, people hide themselves; but when they perish, the righteous flourish.

units.leftText: He who is often rebuked and stiffens his neck will be destroyed suddenly, with no remedy.
units.rightText: A man who remains stiff-necked after much reproof will suddenly be shattered beyond recovery.

units.leftText: When the righteous thrive, the people rejoice; but when the wicked rule, the people groan.
units.rightText: When the righteous flourish, the people rejoice, but when the wicked rule, the people groan.

units.leftText: Whoever loves wisdom brings joy to his father; but a companion of prostitutes squanders his wealth.
units.rightText: A man who loves wisdom brings joy to his father, but a companion of prostitutes squanders his wealth.

units.leftText: The king by justice makes the land stable, but he who takes bribes tears it down.
units.rightText: By justice a king brings stability to the land, but a man who exacts tribute demolishes it.
rightNotes: 29:4 Or who taxes heavily or who takes bribes

units.leftText: A man who flatters his neighbor spreads a net for his feet.
units.rightText: A man who flatters his neighbor spreads a net for his feet.

units.leftText: An evil man is snared by his sin, but the righteous can sing and be glad.
units.rightText: An evil man is caught by his own sin, but a righteous one sings and rejoices.

units.leftText: The righteous care about justice for the poor. The wicked aren’t concerned about knowledge.
units.rightText: The righteous consider the cause of the poor, but the wicked have no regard for such concerns.

units.leftText: Mockers stir up a city, but wise men turn away anger.
units.rightText: Mockers inflame a city, but the wise turn away anger.

units.leftText: If a wise man goes to court with a foolish man, the fool rages or scoffs, and there is no peace.
units.rightText: If a wise man goes to court with a fool, there will be raving and laughing with no resolution.

units.leftText: The bloodthirsty hate a man of integrity; and they seek the life of the upright.
units.rightText: Men of bloodshed hate a blameless man, but the upright care for his life.
rightNotes: 29:10 Or but the upright seek his soul

units.leftText: A fool vents all of his anger, but a wise man brings himself under control.
units.rightText: A fool vents all his anger, but a wise man holds it back.

units.leftText: If a ruler listens to lies, all of his officials are wicked.
units.rightText: If a ruler listens to lies, all his officials will be wicked.

units.leftText: The poor man and the oppressor have this in common: The LORD gives sight to the eyes of both.
units.rightText: The poor man and the oppressor have this in common: The LORD gives light to the eyes of both.

units.leftText: The king who fairly judges the poor, his throne shall be established forever.
units.rightText: A king who judges the poor with fairness— his throne will be established forever.

units.leftText: The rod of correction gives wisdom, but a child left to himself causes shame to his mother.
units.rightText: A rod of correction imparts wisdom, but a child left to himself disgraces his mother.

units.leftText: When the wicked increase, sin increases; but the righteous will see their downfall.
units.rightText: When the wicked thrive, rebellion increases; but the righteous will see their downfall.

units.leftText: Correct your son, and he will give you peace; yes, he will bring delight to your soul.
units.rightText: Discipline your son, and he will give you rest; he will bring delight to your soul.

units.leftText: Where there is no revelation, the people cast off restraint; but one who keeps the law is blessed.
units.rightText: Where there is no vision, the people cast off restraint; but blessed is he who keeps the Law.

units.leftText: A servant can’t be corrected by words. Though he understands, yet he will not respond.
units.rightText: A servant cannot be corrected by words alone; though he understands, he will not respond.

units.leftText: Do you see a man who is hasty in his words? There is more hope for a fool than for him.
units.rightText: Do you see a man who speaks in haste? There is more hope for a fool than for him.

units.leftText: He who pampers his servant from youth will have him become a son in the end.
units.rightText: A servant pampered from his youth will bring grief in the end.

units.leftText: An angry man stirs up strife, and a wrathful man abounds in sin.
units.rightText: An angry man stirs up dissension, and a hot-tempered man abounds in transgression.

units.leftText: A man’s pride brings him low, but one of lowly spirit gains honor.
units.rightText: A man’s pride will bring him low, but a humble spirit will obtain honor.

units.leftText: Whoever is an accomplice of a thief is an enemy of his own soul. He takes an oath, but dares not testify.
units.rightText: A partner to a thief hates his own soul; he receives the oath but does not testify.

units.leftText: The fear of man proves to be a snare, but whoever puts his trust in the LORD is kept safe.
units.rightText: The fear of man is a snare, but whoever trusts in the LORD is set securely on high.

units.leftText: Many seek the ruler’s favor, but a man’s justice comes from the LORD.
units.rightText: Many seek the ruler’s favor, but a man receives justice from the LORD.

units.leftText: A dishonest man detests the righteous, and the upright in their ways detest the wicked.
units.rightText: An unjust man is detestable to the righteous, and one whose way is upright is detestable to the wicked.

units.leftText: The words of Agur the son of Jakeh, the revelation: the man says to Ithiel, to Ithiel and Ucal:
units.rightText: These are the words of Agur son of Jakeh — the burden that this man declared to Ithiel: “I am weary, O God, and worn out.
rightNotes: 30:1 Or declared to Ithiel: “I am weary, O God, but I can prevail. (revocalizations); Hebrew declared to Ithiel—to Ithiel and Ucal:

units.leftText: “Surely I am the most ignorant man, and don’t have a man’s understanding.
units.rightText: Surely I am the most ignorant of men, and I lack the understanding of a man.

units.leftText: I have not learned wisdom, neither do I have the knowledge of the Holy One.
units.rightText: I have not learned wisdom, and I have no knowledge of the Holy One.

units.leftText: Who has ascended up into heaven, and descended? Who has gathered the wind in his fists? Who has bound the waters in his garment? Who has established all the ends of the earth? What is his name, and what is his son’s name, if you know?
units.rightText: Who has ascended to heaven and come down? Who has gathered the wind in His hands? Who has bound up the waters in His cloak? Who has established all the ends of the earth? What is His name, and what is the name of His Son— surely you know!

units.leftText: “Every word of God is flawless. He is a shield to those who take refuge in him.
units.rightText: Every word of God is flawless; He is a shield to those who take refuge in Him.

units.leftText: Don’t you add to his words, lest he reprove you, and you be found a liar.
units.rightText: Do not add to His words, lest He rebuke you and prove you a liar.

units.leftText: “Two things I have asked of you. Don’t deny me before I die.
units.rightText: Two things I ask of You — do not refuse me before I die:

units.leftText: Remove far from me falsehood and lies. Give me neither poverty nor riches. Feed me with the food that is needful for me,
units.rightText: Keep falsehood and deceitful words far from me. Give me neither poverty nor riches; feed me with the bread that is my portion.

units.leftText: lest I be full, deny you, and say, ‘Who is the LORD?’ or lest I be poor, and steal, and so dishonor the name of my God.
units.rightText: Otherwise, I may have too much and deny You, saying, ‘Who is the LORD?’ Or I may become poor and steal, profaning the name of my God.

units.leftText: “Don’t slander a servant to his master, lest he curse you, and you be held guilty.
units.rightText: Do not slander a servant to his master, or he will curse you, and you will bear the guilt.

units.leftText: There is a generation that curses their father, and doesn’t bless their mother.
units.rightText: There is a generation of those who curse their fathers and do not bless their mothers.

units.leftText: There is a generation that is pure in their own eyes, yet are not washed from their filthiness.
units.rightText: There is a generation of those who are pure in their own eyes and yet unwashed of their filth.

units.leftText: There is a generation, oh how lofty are their eyes! Their eyelids are lifted up.
units.rightText: There is a generation— how haughty are their eyes and pretentious are their glances —

units.leftText: There is a generation whose teeth are like swords, and their jaws like knives, to devour the poor from the earth, and the needy from among men.
units.rightText: there is a generation whose teeth are swords and whose jaws are knives, devouring the oppressed from the earth and the needy from among men.

units.leftText: “The leech has two daughters: ‘Give, give.’ “There are three things that are never satisfied; four that don’t say, ‘Enough!’:
units.rightText: The leech has two daughters: Give and Give. There are three things that are never satisfied, four that never say, ‘Enough!’:

units.leftText: Sheol, the barren womb, the earth that is not satisfied with water, and the fire that doesn’t say, ‘Enough!’
units.rightText: Sheol, the barren womb, land never satisfied with water, and fire that never says, ‘Enough!’
leftNotes: 30:16 Sheol is the place of the dead.

units.leftText: “The eye that mocks at his father, and scorns obedience to his mother, the ravens of the valley shall pick it out, the young eagles shall eat it.
units.rightText: As for the eye that mocks a father and scorns obedience to a mother, may the ravens of the valley pluck it out and young vultures devour it.

units.leftText: “There are three things which are too amazing for me, four which I don’t understand:
units.rightText: There are three things too wonderful for me, four that I cannot understand:

units.leftText: The way of an eagle in the air, the way of a serpent on a rock, the way of a ship in the middle of the sea, and the way of a man with a maiden.
units.rightText: the way of an eagle in the sky, the way of a snake on a rock, the way of a ship at sea, and the way of a man with a maiden.

units.leftText: “So is the way of an adulterous woman: She eats and wipes her mouth, and says, ‘I have done nothing wrong.’
units.rightText: This is the way of an adulteress: She eats and wipes her mouth and says, ‘I have done nothing wrong.’

units.leftText: “For three things the earth trembles, and under four, it can’t bear up:
units.rightText: Under three things the earth trembles, under four it cannot bear up:

units.leftText: For a servant when he is king, a fool when he is filled with food,
units.rightText: a servant who becomes king, a fool who is filled with food,

units.leftText: for an unloved woman when she is married, and a servant who is heir to her mistress.
units.rightText: an unloved woman who marries, and a maidservant who supplants her mistress.

units.leftText: “There are four things which are little on the earth, but they are exceedingly wise:
units.rightText: Four things on earth are small, yet they are exceedingly wise:

units.leftText: The ants are not a strong people, yet they provide their food in the summer.
units.rightText: The ants are creatures of little strength, yet they store up their food in the summer;

units.leftText: The hyraxes are but a feeble folk, yet make they their houses in the rocks.
units.rightText: the rock badgers are creatures of little power, yet they make their homes in the rocks;
rightNotes: 30:26 Or the coneys or the hyraxes

units.leftText: The locusts have no king, yet they advance in ranks.
units.rightText: the locusts have no king, yet they all advance in formation;

units.leftText: You can catch a lizard with your hands, yet it is in kings’ palaces.
units.rightText: and the lizard can be caught in one’s hands, yet it is found in the palaces of kings.

units.leftText: “There are three things which are stately in their march, four which are stately in going:
units.rightText: There are three things that are stately in their stride, and four that are impressive in their walk:

units.leftText: The lion, which is mightiest among animals, and doesn’t turn away for any;
units.rightText: a lion, mighty among beasts, refusing to retreat before anything;

units.leftText: the greyhound; the male goat; and the king against whom there is no rising up.
units.rightText: a strutting rooster; a he-goat; and a king with his army around him.
rightNotes: 30:31 Or a king against whom there is no rising up

units.leftText: “If you have done foolishly in lifting up yourself, or if you have thought evil, put your hand over your mouth.
units.rightText: If you have foolishly exalted yourself or if you have plotted evil, put your hand over your mouth.

units.leftText: For as the churning of milk produces butter, and the wringing of the nose produces blood, so the forcing of wrath produces strife.”
units.rightText: For as the churning of milk yields butter, and the twisting of the nose draws blood, so the stirring of anger brings forth strife.”

units.leftText: The words of King Lemuel—the revelation which his mother taught him:
units.rightText: These are the words of King Lemuel — the burden that his mother taught him:

units.leftText: “Oh, my son! Oh, son of my womb! Oh, son of my vows!
units.rightText: What shall I say, O my son? What, O son of my womb? What, O son of my vows?
rightNotes: 31:2 Or What or What are you doing

units.leftText: Don’t give your strength to women, nor your ways to that which destroys kings.
units.rightText: Do not spend your strength on women or your vigor on those who ruin kings.

units.leftText: It is not for kings, Lemuel, it is not for kings to drink wine, nor for princes to say, ‘Where is strong drink?’
units.rightText: It is not for kings, O Lemuel, it is not for kings to drink wine, or for rulers to crave strong drink,

units.leftText: lest they drink, and forget the law, and pervert the justice due to anyone who is afflicted.
units.rightText: lest they drink and forget what is decreed, depriving all the oppressed of justice.

units.leftText: Give strong drink to him who is ready to perish, and wine to the bitter in soul.
units.rightText: Give strong drink to one who is perishing, and wine to the bitter in soul.

units.leftText: Let him drink, and forget his poverty, and remember his misery no more.
units.rightText: Let him drink and forget his poverty, and remember his misery no more.

units.leftText: Open your mouth for the mute, in the cause of all who are left desolate.
units.rightText: Open your mouth for those with no voice, for the cause of all the dispossessed.

units.leftText: Open your mouth, judge righteously, and serve justice to the poor and needy.”
units.rightText: Open your mouth, judge righteously, and defend the cause of the poor and needy. The Virtues of a Noble Woman

units.leftText: Who can find a worthy woman? For her value is far above rubies.
units.rightText: A wife of noble character, who can find? She is far more precious than rubies.
leftNotes: 31:10 Proverbs 31:10-31 form an acrostic, with each verse starting with each letter of the Hebrew alphabet, in order.
rightNotes: 31:10 Verses 10–31 are an acrostic poem, each verse beginning with the successive letters of the Hebrew alphabet.

units.leftText: The heart of her husband trusts in her. He shall have no lack of gain.
units.rightText: The heart of her husband trusts in her, and he lacks nothing of value.

units.leftText: She does him good, and not harm, all the days of her life.
units.rightText: She brings him good and not harm all the days of her life.

units.leftText: She seeks wool and flax, and works eagerly with her hands.
units.rightText: She selects wool and flax and works with eager hands.

units.leftText: She is like the merchant ships. She brings her bread from afar.
units.rightText: She is like the merchant ships, bringing her food from afar.

units.leftText: She rises also while it is yet night, gives food to her household, and portions for her servant girls.
units.rightText: She rises while it is still night to provide food for her household and portions for her maidservants.

units.leftText: She considers a field, and buys it. With the fruit of her hands, she plants a vineyard.
units.rightText: She appraises a field and buys it; from her earnings she plants a vineyard.

units.leftText: She arms her waist with strength, and makes her arms strong.
units.rightText: She girds herself with strength and shows that her arms are strong.
rightNotes: 31:17 Hebrew She girds her loins

units.leftText: She perceives that her merchandise is profitable. Her lamp doesn’t go out by night.
units.rightText: She sees that her gain is good, and her lamp is not extinguished at night.

units.leftText: She lays her hands to the distaff, and her hands hold the spindle.
units.rightText: She stretches out her hands to the distaff and grasps the spindle with her fingers.

units.leftText: She opens her arms to the poor; yes, she extends her hands to the needy.
units.rightText: She opens her arms to the poor and reaches out her hands to the needy.

units.leftText: She is not afraid of the snow for her household, for all her household are clothed with scarlet.
units.rightText: When it snows, she has no fear for her household, for they are all clothed in scarlet.
rightNotes: 31:21 Or doubly clothed

units.leftText: She makes for herself carpets of tapestry. Her clothing is fine linen and purple.
units.rightText: She makes coverings for her bed; her clothing is fine linen and purple.

units.leftText: Her husband is respected in the gates, when he sits among the elders of the land.
units.rightText: Her husband is known at the city gates, where he sits among the elders of the land.

units.leftText: She makes linen garments and sells them, and delivers sashes to the merchant.
units.rightText: She makes linen garments and sells them; she delivers sashes to the merchants.

units.leftText: Strength and dignity are her clothing. She laughs at the time to come.
units.rightText: Strength and honor are her clothing, and she can laugh at the days to come.

units.leftText: She opens her mouth with wisdom. Kind instruction is on her tongue.
units.rightText: She opens her mouth with wisdom, and faithful instruction is on her tongue.

units.leftText: She looks well to the ways of her household, and doesn’t eat the bread of idleness.
units.rightText: She watches over the affairs of her household and does not eat the bread of idleness.

units.leftText: Her children rise up and call her blessed. Her husband also praises her:
units.rightText: Her children rise up and call her blessed; her husband praises her as well:

units.leftText: “Many women do noble things, but you excel them all.”
units.rightText: “Many daughters have done noble things, but you surpass them all!”

units.leftText: Charm is deceitful, and beauty is vain; but a woman who fears the LORD, she shall be praised.
units.rightText: Charm is deceptive and beauty is fleeting, but a woman who fears the LORD is to be praised.

units.leftText: Give her of the fruit of her hands! Let her works praise her in the gates!
units.rightText: Give her the fruit of her hands, and let her works praise her at the gates.
